  legend. Yellow, Bright teal and Gray are light against White, so labels are what make them
  readable, and they help anyone who cannot tell the colors apart.
- Keep to four series or fewer. Fold the rest into Other, or split the chart.
- Use one value axis. Two measures on different scales belong in two charts.
- Never use Magenta for a series: it means something is wrong.

## Type styles

Use the built-in styles in the templates instead of formatting text by hand. Styles keep a long
document consistent, build the table of contents and tell screen readers how the document is
organized.

### Documents (Word and Google Docs)

| Style | Font | Size | Color | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Title | Oswald | 32 pt | Deep teal | Capitals, once per document |
| Subtitle | Lato | 14 pt | Slate | |
| Heading 1 | Lato Bold | 20 pt | Ink | Sections |
| Heading 2 | Lato Bold | 15 pt | Ink | Parts of a section |
| Heading 3 | Lato Bold | 12.5 pt | Ink | Rarely needed |
| Normal | Lato | 11 pt | Ink | Line spacing 1.4, 8 pt after each paragraph |

### Slides (PowerPoint and Google Slides)

| Style | Font | Size | Color |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Title on a white slide | Oswald, capitals | 40 pt | Ink |
| Title on a Deep teal slide | Oswald, capitals | 54 pt | White |
| Body, first level | Lato | 24 pt | Ink |
| Body, second level | Lato | 20 pt | Slate |
| Smallest text, such as a source | Lato | 18 pt | Slate |

Microsoft [recommends 18 pt or larger](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/powerpoint/make-your-powerpoint-presentations-accessible-to-people-with-disabilities)
for slide text. Never go smaller.

### Spreadsheets (Excel and Google Sheets)

| Style | Font | Size | Color |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sheet title | Oswald, capitals | 24 pt | Deep teal |
| Header row | Lato Bold | 11 pt | White on Deep teal |
| Cells | Lato | 11 pt | Ink, with Mist stripes |

### Case

Only Oswald titles are in capitals. Everything else, headings and table headers included, is in
sentence case: a capital first letter and lower case after it, except for names.

## The logo

Use the logo files in [`assets/logos`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-office/blob/v1.0.0/assets/logos), never a copy from a website or an old
file.

| Background | Logo |
| --- | --- |
| White or a light color | Full color: `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png` |
| Deep teal, a dark color or a dark photo | White: `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png` |
| One color printing | Black: `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-black.png` |

- Put the logo once per page or slide, in a corner. The templates place it for you.
- Leave clear space around it equal to half its height.
- Never stretch, recolor, outline or redraw it, and never put the full color logo on Deep teal.
- In a document, keep the horizontal logo at least a third of an inch (8 mm) tall so the wordmark
  stays readable. Use the MC monogram alone only where MassChallenge is already named.

The [brand guidelines](/brand/reference/)
have the full logo rules.

## Layout

- **Leave space.** White space makes a page easier to read. Do not fill every corner.
- **Align to the margins.** Line up text, images and charts on the same left edge.
- **One idea per slide, one table per sheet, one purpose per document.**
- **Round the corners of photos and panels** slightly, about 0.12 inch (3 mm), as the website does
  with 12 pixels. Logos and charts stay square.
- **Use real lists.** Use the bullet and numbering buttons, never typed dashes or asterisks.

## Writing

Documents sound like the rest of MassChallenge: bold and human, direct and plain spoken.

- Put the point first: the decision, the ask or the takeaway.
- Use short sentences and everyday words. Write "we" for MassChallenge and "you" for the reader.
- Make a slide title say the takeaway, not the topic: "Applications grew in every program", not
  "Applications".
- Skip buzzwords such as leverage, seamless and robust, and skip exclamation marks.
- Use commas, colons and periods. Do not use em dashes or en dashes.

## Accessibility

Everything we send should work for people who use screen readers, magnifiers or high contrast
settings.

- Use the built-in title, heading and list styles so the structure is real, not just visual.
- Give every photo, chart and diagram alt text that says what it shows. Mark purely decorative
  images as decorative.
- Give every slide a unique title, even if you hide it.
- Run the checker before you share: in Word, PowerPoint and Excel choose **Review**, then
  [**Check Accessibility**](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/improve-accessibility-with-the-accessibility-checker-a16f6de0-2f39-4a2b-8bd8-5ad801426c7f).
  Google Docs, Sheets and Slides have no built-in checker, so check headings, alt text and slide
  titles by hand.
- Use link text that says where it goes, such as "the application guide", never "click here".

## Photography and video

People are at the heart of how MassChallenge looks. The
[photography and video guide](/guidelines/photography/) covers choosing, treating and placing photos and
videos, from your own event photos to licensed stock.

# Google Docs

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/office/google-docs/

This guide covers memos, reports and proposals in Google Docs. Read the
[foundations](/office/foundations/) first, and the [Word guide](/office/word/) for structure, lists and tables:
the same rules apply, and this page covers what is different in Google Docs.

## Start from the template

Google Docs has no template file of its own to download, so the Propellant template comes as a
Word file that Docs converts.

1. Download [`propellant-document.docx`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-office/raw/v1.0.0/templates/word/propellant-document.docx).
2. In Google Drive, choose **New**, then **File upload**, and pick it.
3. Open it, choose **File**, then **Save as Google Docs**. Work in the Google Docs copy.

If your organization has added Propellant to the Docs template gallery, choose **File**, then
**New**, then **From template gallery** instead. [Installing the templates](/office/templates/) explains
how an administrator sets that up, and how to share a "make a copy" link.

Google does not publish a list of what changes when a Word file is converted, so check the result.
The styles, colors, logo and table come across; review the header, footer and page numbers once.

## Fonts

Lato and Oswald are both available in Google Docs. If they are not in your font menu yet, open the
font menu, choose **More fonts**, search for each one and select it. They then stay in your menu.

## Styles

Google Docs calls styles "paragraph styles". The converted template already has them set. Pick
them from the style menu on the toolbar, which shows **Normal text** by default.

| Google Docs style | Propellant style |
| --- | --- |
| Title | Oswald, 32 pt, Deep teal, capitals |
| Subtitle | Lato, 14 pt, Slate |
| Heading 1 | Lato Bold, 20 pt, Ink |
| Heading 2 | Lato Bold, 15 pt, Ink |
| Heading 3 | Lato Bold, 12.5 pt, Ink |
| Normal text | Lato, 11 pt, Ink, line spacing 1.4 |

If a style looks wrong in a document that did not start from the template, fix one example by
hand, select it, and choose **Update "Heading 1" to match** from the style menu. To make the
Propellant styles your default for every new document, open the style menu, choose **Options**,
then **Save as my default styles**.

Google Docs cannot make text capitals with a style setting, so type the Title in capitals.

## Page setup

- Choose **File**, then **Page setup**: Letter, one inch margins, and **Pages** rather than
  **Pageless** for anything that will be printed or shared as a PDF.
- Use **Pageless** for working documents that stay in Docs, such as meeting notes.

## Tables and callouts

- Insert tables with **Insert**, then **Table**. Set the header row background to Deep teal
  `#044451` with White bold text, and add Mist `#F3F6F7` to alternate rows if the table is long.
- To pin the header row when a table crosses pages, right click it, choose **Table properties**,
  then **Pin header rows**.
- For a callout, insert a one cell table with a Pale teal `#D9F6FA` background and no border, or
  copy the callout from the template.

Add custom colors once with **Custom** in any color menu; Docs remembers them under **Custom**.

## Photos

- Insert photos with **Insert**, then **Image**, and choose **In line** so they move with the
  text.
- Add alt text: right click the image and choose **Alt text**.
- Use Google's own image search only for ideas. Use photos from our libraries, as the
  [photography guide](/guidelines/photography/) explains.

## Before you share

Google Docs has no built-in accessibility checker. Check by hand:

1. Open **View**, then **Show outline**. Every section should appear, in order.
2. Make sure every image has alt text and every link says where it goes.
3. Share with **Viewer** or **Commenter** access unless someone needs to edit.
4. For people outside MassChallenge, send a PDF with **File**, then **Download**, then **PDF
   document**.

# Google Sheets

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/office/google-sheets/

This guide covers trackers, budgets and shared data in Google Sheets. Read the
[foundations](/office/foundations/) first, and the [Excel guide](/office/excel/) for sheets, numbers and
charts: the same rules apply, and this page covers what is different in Google Sheets.

## Start from the template

1. Download [`propellant-workbook.xlsx`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-office/raw/v1.0.0/templates/excel/propellant-workbook.xlsx).
2. In Google Drive, choose **New**, then **File upload**, and pick it.
3. Open it and choose **File**, then **Save as Google Sheets**. Work in the Google Sheets copy.

The header row and Mist stripes are set as cell formatting, so they come across as they are. Check
the chart once after converting.

If your organization has added Propellant to the Sheets template gallery, choose it from
**Template gallery** on the Sheets home page instead. See [installing the templates](/office/templates/).

## Theme

Google Sheets has its own theme for fonts and chart colors.

1. Choose **Format**, then **Theme**.
2. Choose **Customize** and set the font to **Lato**, the text color to Ink `#1E282B`, and the
   accents in the Propellant order: Teal `#065E6F`, Yellow `#FFC801`, Slate `#4B575B`, Bright
   teal `#0FACBD`, Deep teal `#044451` and Gray `#848F92`. Set links to Teal `#065E6F`.

Charts and new tables then pick up the brand colors. If Lato is not in the font list, add it from
**More fonts** in the toolbar's font menu first.

## Titles and headers

| Element | Style |
| --- | --- |
| Sheet title | Oswald, 24 pt, Deep teal, typed in capitals |
| Header row | Lato Bold, 11 pt, White on Deep teal `#044451` |
| Cells | Lato, 11 pt, Ink |
| Alternate rows | Mist `#F3F6F7` |

To get banded rows on new data, select it and choose **Format**, then **Alternating colors**, then
set the header to Deep teal and the second color to Mist. You can also use **Format**, then
**Convert to table**, which adds filters and column types.

Freeze the header row with **View**, then **Freeze**, then **1 row**.

## Status

Use a dropdown for status (**Insert**, then **Dropdown**) with words such as On track, At risk and
Late. You can color the dropdown chips, but keep the word: never show status by color alone.

## Charts

- Insert charts with **Insert**, then **Chart**. With the theme set, they use the brand colors.
- In the chart editor's **Customize** tab, turn on data labels when there is more than one series,
  set the chart and axis titles, and remove the chart border.
- Follow the chart rules in the [foundations](/office/foundations/#charts).
- Add alt text: select the chart, open the three dot menu, and choose **Alt text**.

## Sharing

- Share with **Viewer** access by default. Protect ranges people should not edit with **Data**,
  then **Protect sheets and ranges**.
- Google Sheets has no built-in accessibility checker. Check that headers are in the first row,
  there are no merged cells in tables, and status is written as words.
- For people outside MassChallenge, download a PDF or an Excel file from **File**, then
  **Download**.

# Google Slides

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/office/google-slides/

This guide covers presentations in Google Slides. Read the [foundations](/office/foundations/) first,
and the [PowerPoint guide](/office/powerpoint/) for layouts, titles, text and charts: the same rules
apply, and this page covers what is different in Google Slides.

## Start from the template

1. Download [`propellant-presentation.pptx`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-office/raw/v1.0.0/templates/powerpoint/propellant-presentation.pptx).
2. In Google Drive, choose **New**, then **File upload**, and pick it.
3. Open it and choose **File**, then **Save as Google Slides**. Work in the Google Slides copy.

If your organization has added Propellant to the Slides template gallery or made it the default
theme, use that instead. [Installing the templates](/office/templates/) explains both.

### Bringing an existing deck onto the brand

1. Open the deck and choose **Slide**, then **Change theme**.
2. Choose **Import theme** at the bottom of the panel, and pick the Propellant presentation from
   Drive or upload the `.pptx`.
3. Select the Propellant theme. Then select each slide and set its layout with **Slide**, then
   **Apply layout**.

Google does not publish a list of what changes when a PowerPoint file is converted. Check the
title slide, a section slide and a content slide after converting.

## Slide size

Choose **File**, then **Page setup**, and keep **Widescreen 16:9**. A converted Propellant deck
keeps PowerPoint's 13.333 by 7.5 inch size, which is right; do not change it once you have
started, because the layouts will shift.

## Fonts and theme colors

- Lato and Oswald are available in Google Slides. If they are not in your font menu, choose
  **More fonts** and add them.
- Check the theme colors with **Slide**, then **Edit theme**, then **Colors**. The Propellant
  colors appear as Text and background, Accent 1 to 6 and Link. Pick colors from the theme
  section of any color menu, never a custom color.

## Editing the layouts

Google calls the master slides the **theme builder**: choose **Slide**, then **Edit theme**. The
first slide in the left panel is the master; the rest are the layouts. The converted template
already carries the Propellant master, with the Deep teal title and section layouts and the logo.
Change layouts here only to fix something for every slide, and keep the original Propellant theme
untouched in a separate copy.

## Photos and video

- Insert photos with **Insert**, then **Image**. To crop, double click the image and drag the
  black crop handles; to choose a shape, use the arrow beside the crop button.
- Add alt text: right click the image and choose **Alt text**.
- Insert video with **Insert**, then **Video**, from YouTube or Drive. Under **Format options**,
  set it to play on click and turn on captions if they exist.
- Follow the [photography guide](/guidelines/photography/).

## Presenting and sharing

- Google Slides has no built-in accessibility checker. Check that every slide has a title (open
  **View**, then **Grid view**, to see them all), every image has alt text and the text is 18 pt
  or larger.
- Turn on captions while presenting with the **CC** button in the presenter toolbar.
- For people outside MassChallenge, share a view only link or download a PDF with **File**, then
  **Download**, then **PDF document**.

# PowerPoint

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/office/powerpoint/

This guide covers pitch decks, program updates, workshop slides and event presentations in
Microsoft PowerPoint. Read the [foundations](/office/foundations/) first: they set the colors, fonts and
voice this guide applies.

## Start from the template

1. Install [`propellant-presentation.potx`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-office/raw/v1.0.0/templates/powerpoint/propellant-presentation.potx)
   as described in [installing the templates](/office/templates/).
2. In PowerPoint, choose **File**, then **New**, then **Personal** (or **Shared**), and pick
   **Propellant presentation**.
3. The template opens with eight sample slides that show every layout. Keep the ones you need,
   delete the rest, and add new slides with **Home**, then **New Slide**.

Moving an existing deck to Propellant? Choose **Design**, then the arrow beside the themes, then
**Browse for Themes**, and pick [`Propellant.thmx`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-office/raw/v1.0.0/templates/powerpoint/Propellant.thmx). That
switches the colors and fonts. Then reapply each slide's layout from **Home**, then **Layout**.

## Slide size

Slides are widescreen 16:9, 13.333 by 7.5 inches, PowerPoint's default. Keep it: it fits every
screen and video call. Do not switch to 4:3.

## Layouts

Always pick a layout instead of drawing your own text boxes. Layouts keep titles in the same
place on every slide, and screen readers use the title placeholder to name each slide.

| Layout | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| Title Slide | The first slide. Deep teal, white logo, title in capitals, subtitle in Bright teal. |
| Title and Content | Most slides: a title and up to five bullets, a chart, a table or a photo. |
| Section Header | Dividing a long deck into parts. Deep teal, like the title slide. Also the closing slide. |
| Two Content | Before and after, or two options side by side. |
| Comparison | Two options, each with a short heading. |
| Title Only | A big number, a quote or a diagram you place yourself. |
| Picture with Caption | One photo filling the left half, with a title and caption on the right. |
| Blank | A full bleed photo or video. |

Use Deep teal slides only for the title, section breaks and the closing slide. Everything in
between is white, so the Deep teal moments stand out.

## Titles

- Make every title say the takeaway: "Applications grew in every program", not "Applications".
- Keep titles to one line, about 40 characters. The template sets them in Oswald capitals; type
  them in sentence case and the style does the rest.
- Give every slide a different title, even if you then hide it. PowerPoint's accessibility
  checker flags a missing title as an error.

## Text

- One idea per slide. If you need more than five bullets, split the slide.
- Keep bullets short, without full stops on single lines, and one level deep where you can.
- Never shrink text below 18 pt to make it fit. Microsoft
  [recommends 18 pt or larger](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/powerpoint/make-your-powerpoint-presentations-accessible-to-people-with-disabilities).
  Cut words instead.
- Put detail in the speaker notes, not on the slide.

## Big numbers and quotes

The two Title Only samples show how:

- **A big number:** the number in Oswald at about 120 pt in Deep teal, with one line underneath
  saying what it means and where it comes from. Always give the source.
- **A quote:** the quote in Lato at about 36 pt with real curly quote marks, and the person's
  name, role and company below in Slate. Only quote people who agreed to be quoted.

## Charts

- Insert charts with **Insert**, then **Chart**, so they take their colors from the theme.
- Use the chart rules in the [foundations](/office/foundations/#charts): one series in Teal, labels on
  the chart when there are more, four series at most, one axis.
- Remove what does not help: gridlines down to a few light ones, no 3D, no shadows, no chart
  border.
- Put the takeaway in the slide title and the source in small text below the chart.

## Photos and video

- Use photos that fill the frame: the Picture with Caption layout, or a full bleed photo on a
  Blank slide.
- When you crop, crop on purpose: keep faces and heads whole and leave the people looking into
  the slide. Use **Picture Format**, then **Crop**, then **Fill**, and drag the photo to place it.
- Put text on a photo only over a calm, dark area, or on a Deep teal band. Use the white logo on
  dark photos.
- For video, insert the file or a link with **Insert**, then **Video**, add captions, and set it
  to start when clicked, not automatically.
- Follow the [photography guide](/guidelines/photography/), including alt text for every photo.

## The logo

The template places the logo for you: the white logo at the top left of Deep teal slides and the
full color logo at the bottom right of white slides. Do not add another logo, and do not move it
into the content area. On a full bleed photo slide, the full color logo can disappear into the
photo: right click the slide, choose **Format Background**, check **Hide background graphics**, and
place the white logo from [`assets/logos`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-office/blob/v1.0.0/assets/logos) in a dark corner instead.

## Presenting and sharing

1. Run **Review**, then **Check Accessibility**, and fix every error and warning.
2. Check the reading order of busy slides in the **Reading Order** pane.
3. To send the deck to someone outside MassChallenge, send a PDF, or
   [embed the fonts](/office/foundations/#sending-files-outside-masschallenge) if they need to edit it.
4. Before presenting on someone else's computer, check that Lato and Oswald are installed there,
   or bring a PDF.

## Things to avoid

- Animations other than a simple Appear or Fade, and slide transitions other than Fade.
- Text in Teal, except links, and Teal text on Deep teal.
- Logos, icons or photos copied from a web search.
- Busy backgrounds, gradients, shadows and outlines on text.
- Slides read word for word. If the slide says it all, the presenter has nothing to add.

# Installing the templates

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/office/templates/

The templates are in the [`templates`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-office/blob/v1.0.0/templates) folder. Each comes in two forms: a template
file for Microsoft Office (`.dotx`, `.potx`, `.xltx`) that opens a fresh copy every time, and a
regular file (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`) for Google Workspace and for opening directly.

| Template | Office | Google Workspace |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Document | `word/propellant-document.dotx` | `word/propellant-document.docx` |
| Presentation | `powerpoint/propellant-presentation.potx` | `powerpoint/propellant-presentation.pptx` |
| Workbook | `excel/propellant-workbook.xltx` | `excel/propellant-workbook.xlsx` |
| Theme only | `powerpoint/Propellant.thmx` | Not needed |

Install [Lato and Oswald](/office/foundations/#getting-the-fonts) first, or Office will show other
fonts.

## For yourself

### Microsoft Office on Windows

1. Download the `.dotx`, `.potx` and `.xltx` files.
2. Save them to your personal templates folder: type `%appdata%\Microsoft\Templates` into the
   File Explorer address bar.
3. In Word, PowerPoint and Excel, choose **File**, then **Options**, then **Save**, and paste the
   same folder into **Default personal templates location**.
4. Choose **File**, then **New**, then **Personal** to find the templates.

Microsoft's page [Where are my custom templates](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/foundations-experiences/where-are-my-custom-templates)
has the details.

### Microsoft Office on Mac

1. Download the template files.
2. Save them to `~/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/User Content/Templates`. In Finder,
   choose **Go**, then **Go to Folder**, and paste that path.
3. Choose **File**, then **New from Template** to find them.

### Microsoft Office on the web

Office on the web cannot open personal templates. Save the `.docx`, `.pptx` or `.xlsx` to
OneDrive, open it, and use **File**, then **Save a copy** before you start, so the original stays
clean.

### Google Workspace

Upload the `.docx`, `.pptx` or `.xlsx` to Drive and choose **File**, then **Save as Google Docs**
(or Slides, or Sheets). Keep that copy as your master and make a copy of it for each new
document. The guides for [Google Docs](/office/google-docs/), [Google Slides](/office/google-slides/) and
[Google Sheets](/office/google-sheets/) cover the details.

## For everyone at MassChallenge

These steps need an administrator.

### Microsoft 365

- **Templates:** a SharePoint administrator can create an
  [organization assets library](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/organization-assets-library)
  for templates and upload the `.dotx`, `.potx` and `.xltx` files. They then appear for everyone
  in Word, PowerPoint and Excel on Windows and Mac, and in PowerPoint on the web, under the
  organization's name. Word and Excel on the web do not show them.
- **Fonts:** the same administrator can
  [publish Lato and Oswald as organization fonts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/support-for-organization-fonts-in-powerpoint-for-the-web)
  so they work in PowerPoint and Word on every platform, including the web, without anyone
  installing them. Both fonts are under the SIL Open Font License, but have the license checked
  for cloud hosting first. Allow up to a day for both to appear.
- **Installing the fonts:** IT can also install Lato and Oswald on every managed computer.

### Google Workspace

- **Template gallery:** an administrator can
  [turn on custom templates](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/drive/turn-custom-drive-templates-on-or-off-for-users)
  in the Admin console under **Apps**, then **Google Workspace**, then **Drive and Docs**, then
  **Templates**. Then submit the converted Google Docs, Slides and Sheets templates to the
  MassChallenge section of the gallery.
- **Default theme:** with organization branding turned on, an administrator can
  [set a default Slides theme](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/drive/what-are-default-templates-and-themes)
  so every new presentation starts with Propellant.
- **Copy links:** for anyone else, share a Google copy of each template and change the end of its
  link from `/edit` to `/copy`. Opening that link makes the person their own copy.

## Updating the templates

The templates are generated by `scripts/build_templates.py` from the Propellant colors, fonts and
logos, so they never drift apart. When the brand changes, the templates are rebuilt and released
together. Replace your installed copies with the files from the latest release.

# Word

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/office/word/

This guide covers memos, reports, proposals, letters and one pagers in Microsoft Word. Read the
[foundations](/office/foundations/) first: they set the colors, fonts and voice this guide applies.

## Start from the template

1. Install [`propellant-document.dotx`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-office/raw/v1.0.0/templates/word/propellant-document.dotx) as described in
   [installing the templates](/office/templates/).
2. In Word, choose **File**, then **New**, then **Personal** (or **Shared** if your organization
   publishes it), and pick **Propellant document**.
3. Replace the sample text. Keep the styles.

The template sets a US Letter page with one inch margins, the logo in the header, page numbers in
the footer, and every style below. It also opens with the same skeleton our documents use: a
title, an italic status line, the author, and an Overview section.

Already have a document? Open it and choose **Design**, then **Themes**, then **Browse for
Themes**, and pick [`Propellant.thmx`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-office/raw/v1.0.0/templates/powerpoint/Propellant.thmx). That switches
the colors and theme fonts. You still need to apply the Propellant styles below.

## Structure

Every document follows the same order so readers always know where to look:

1. **Title** in the Title style, in capitals. Keep it short: what the document is.
2. **Subtitle**, optional: the program, period or audience.
3. **Status line** in italics, such as Status: Draft, and **Author** on the line below.
4. **Overview** as Heading 1: one or two paragraphs with the point, the ask or the decision.
5. **Sections** as Heading 1, with Heading 2 for the parts inside them.

Keep documents short. Most should fit on four pages. If it runs longer, move detail to an
appendix at the end.

## Styles

Use the Styles gallery on the **Home** tab. Never make text look like a heading by making it bold
and big: it will not show in the navigation pane, the table of contents or a screen reader.

| Style | What it looks like | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title | Oswald, 32 pt, Deep teal, capitals | The document title, once |
| Subtitle | Lato, 14 pt, Slate | A short line under the title |
| Heading 1 | Lato Bold, 20 pt, Ink | Sections, including Overview |
| Heading 2 | Lato Bold, 15 pt, Ink | Parts of a section |
| Heading 3 | Lato Bold, 12.5 pt, Ink | Use sparingly |
| Normal | Lato, 11 pt, Ink, line spacing 1.4 | All body text |
| List Bullet, List Number | Lato, 11 pt | Lists |

Headings are in sentence case. Only the Title is in capitals, and the style does that for you, so
type the title normally.

## Lists

- Use the **Bullets** or **Numbering** buttons, never typed dashes.
- Use numbers only when the order matters, such as steps.
- Keep each item to one idea and start it with a capital letter.

## Tables

The sample table in the template shows the style: a Deep teal header row with White bold text,
thin Line `#DBE1E3` rules between rows and Mist on every other row.

- Put the header in the first row and set it to repeat: select the row, choose **Table Layout**,
  then **Repeat Header Rows**.
- Left align text and right align numbers. Give every column the same number of decimals.
- Do not merge cells or leave empty rows for spacing. Screen readers read tables cell by cell.
- If a table runs past half a page, consider putting it in an appendix or an Excel file.

## Callouts

For the one thing a reader must not miss, use a callout: a paragraph with a Pale teal `#D9F6FA`
fill and a Teal left border, as in the template. Copy it from the sample. Use one per page at most.

## Photos and images

- Insert photos with **Insert**, then **Pictures**. Choose **In Line with Text** from **Layout
  Options** so they move with the text.
- Size photos to the full text width or half of it. Do not let text wrap around small photos.
- Add alt text: right click the photo and choose **View Alt Text**.
- Add a caption below with **References**, then **Insert Caption** when the photo needs context.
- Follow the [photography guide](/guidelines/photography/) for choosing photos.

## Headers and footers

The template puts the full color logo at the top left of every page and "MassChallenge | Page"
with the page number at the bottom right. Do not add more to the header. For a confidential
document, add the word Confidential to the footer, never a watermark across the page.

## Before you share

1. Run **Review**, then **Check Accessibility**, and fix every error.
2. Check that the headings show in **View**, then **Navigation Pane**.
3. Fill in **File**, then **Info**, then **Properties**: a title, so screen readers announce it.
4. Send a PDF (**File**, **Save As**, **PDF**) to people who only need to read it. If someone
   outside MassChallenge needs to edit it, [embed the fonts](/office/foundations/#sending-files-outside-masschallenge).

## Things to avoid

- Text in Teal, except links.
- Oswald in body text, lists or tables.
- More than one font size per style, or text formatted by hand instead of with styles.
- Word art, shadows, outlines, gradients and 3D effects.
- Clip art and low resolution logos copied from the web.

# Platforms

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/platforms/

Each platform has its own version of Propellant, in its own repository, with its own releases. They
all follow the same [brand](/brand/) and [guidelines](/guidelines/).

| Platform           | Status    | Repository                                                                              |
| ------------------ | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Web](/web/)       | Available | [`masschallenge/propellant-web`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web)       |
| [Office](/office/) | Available | [`masschallenge/propellant-office`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-office) |

## Adding a platform

A new platform gets its own repository named `propellant-<platform>`, with its guides in a `docs`
folder and a `README.md` that introduces it. Once it has a first release, this site adds it to the
navigation and publishes its guides from each new release.

# Propellant for the web

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/

Propellant is how MassChallenge looks, sounds and works on the web. It is the shared kit our teams
use to build every MassChallenge website and product: our colors and fonts, ready made pieces like
buttons and forms, and the guidance for putting them together. When everyone builds from the same
parts, people get the same clear, accessible experience wherever they meet us.

This repository holds the web version: design tokens (the named colors, sizes and spacing),
React components, an application layout, and the brand and usage guidelines behind them.

Propellant was inspired by Apple's Human Interface Guidelines and Google's Material Design.
Apple and Human Interface Guidelines are trademarks of Apple Inc. Google and Material Design are
trademarks of Google LLC. Propellant is not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by Apple or
Google.

## What is inside

- **Design tokens** for color, type, shape, depth, motion and layout, in light and dark mode. Controls
  grow for touch screens, and motion calms down for people who ask their device to reduce it.
- **Components** for buttons, forms, navigation, menus, messages and tables. Each one works with a
  keyboard, makes sense to screen readers and comes with tests.
- **An application layout** with a sidebar and a toolbar that adapts to narrow windows.
- **The MassChallenge logo** as a component and as image files in three versions.
- **Guidelines** for using Propellant and for the MassChallenge brand.

## Install

```bash
npm install github:masschallenge/propellant-web#v1.1.1
```

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@masschallenge/propellant-web/styles.scoped.css';
@import '@masschallenge/propellant-web/utilities.css';
@source '../node_modules/@masschallenge/propellant-web/src';
```

```tsx


export const Example = () => (
  <div data-propellant>
    <Button>Save changes</Button>
  </div>
);
```

The [usage guide](/web/usage/) walks through apps and sites with a build step. Building in
WordPress, Squarespace or another site builder? The [websites guide](/web/websites/) needs no
install: one stylesheet and a few class names.

## Documentation

- [Usage guide](/web/usage/)
- [Websites and site builders](/web/websites/): WordPress, Squarespace, Webflow, Wix, HubSpot and plain HTML
- [Brand guidelines](/brand/reference/), including logo usage
- [Images and uploads](/guidelines/images/): how to handle photos and logos people upload
- [Contributing](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web/blob/v1.1.1/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Changelog](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web/blob/v1.1.1/CHANGELOG.md)

The documentation site and Storybook run locally:

```bash
yarn site         # documentation site with live examples
yarn storybook    # component workshop on http://localhost:6006
yarn site:build   # the documentation site as one HTML file in site/dist
```

## Getting help

- **Bugs, questions and ideas:** open an issue on GitHub. The [contributing guide](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web/blob/v1.1.1/CONTRIBUTING.md)
  explains how we handle them.
- **Security problems:** report them privately, as described in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web/blob/v1.1.1/SECURITY.md).
- **Using the MassChallenge name or logo:** read the [brand guidelines](/brand/reference/). For
  anything they do not cover, contact MassChallenge through
  [masschallenge.org](https://masschallenge.org).

## Development

```bash
yarn install
yarn build              # token stylesheets in dist
yarn lint
yarn typecheck
yarn test               # unit tests
yarn test:stories       # interaction tests for every story in Chromium
yarn test:vr            # visual regression against vr/__screenshots__
```

Visual regression baselines are recorded in the `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.0-noble`
container so they match continuous integration:

```bash
yarn build-storybook
docker run --rm --ipc=host -v "$PWD":/work -w /work mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.0-noble \
  bash -lc "npx playwright test --config playwright.vr.config.ts"
```

and logos are trademarks of MassChallenge, Inc. and are not covered by that license; see
[the brand guidelines](/brand/reference/) for how they may be used. The fonts are licensed under the

# Using Propellant

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/usage/

Propellant gives your product the MassChallenge look, ready to build with: our colors, type and
spacing, plus the buttons, forms and app frame that screens are made of. Install it once and every
page starts on brand, with keyboard support and contrast already handled, so your team spends its
time on the product instead of rebuilding the same pieces.

## What you get

Propellant comes in two layers. Tokens are our design decisions given names, such as `--tint` for
the color of links and actions or `--corner-lg` for a rounded corner. Any website can use them.
Components are ready made React pieces, such as `Button` and `AppShell`, built from those tokens.

Because every product draws from the same source, MassChallenge looks and works the same
everywhere, and a change we make here reaches every team that installs the next version. You can
start small, too: Propellant only styles the parts of a page you hand to it.

## Pick your setup

Find the row that matches what you are building. The rest of this guide follows it.

| You are building | Use |
| --- | --- |
| A site in WordPress, Squarespace, Webflow, Wix, HubSpot or plain HTML | One stylesheet and a few class names, no install. Follow the [websites guide](/web/websites/). |
| A React application | Components, tokens and the text style utilities. |
| A website styled with Tailwind CSS | Tokens and utilities, plus components where the site uses React. |
| A website with its own CSS | Tokens only, through CSS custom properties. |

Propellant needs Node 22 or later and, for components, React 19.

## Install

Install the package from GitHub at a released version:

```bash
npm install github:masschallenge/propellant-web#v1.1.1
```

```bash
yarn add github:masschallenge/propellant-web#v1.1.1
```

The package is published as `@masschallenge/propellant-web`.

## React applications

### 1. Load the styles

Our components are styled with Tailwind CSS 4. In your global stylesheet, import Tailwind, the
scoped tokens and the utilities. Then point Tailwind at the package source with `@source`, so it
generates the classes the components use:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@masschallenge/propellant-web/styles.scoped.css';
@import '@masschallenge/propellant-web/utilities.css';
@source '../node_modules/@masschallenge/propellant-web/src';
```

Adjust the `@source` path so it is relative to the stylesheet.

The stylesheet brings the Propellant Sans and Oswald fonts with it, so there is nothing else to
load.

### 2. Compile the package

Propellant ships as TypeScript source, which your build tool turns into JavaScript. Vite does this
with no setup. In Next.js, add the package to `transpilePackages`:

```js
const nextConfig = {
  transpilePackages: ['@masschallenge/propellant-web'],
};

export default nextConfig;
```

### 3. Render inside the boundary

Tokens apply only inside an element with the `data-propellant` attribute. Put it near the root of
the part of the page Propellant should style:

```tsx


export const Example = () => (
  <div data-propellant>
    <Button>Save changes</Button>
  </div>
);
```

Everything outside the boundary keeps its existing styles, so a product can move to Propellant one
page at a time.

### 4. Frame the application

Signed in applications use `AppShell`: a `Sidebar` for places, a `Toolbar` for context and one main
area for the page. On windows narrower than 1024px, the sidebar becomes an overlay that opens from
a toolbar button.

```tsx

  AppShell,
  Logo,
  Sidebar,
  SidebarItem,
  SidebarSection,
  Toolbar,
} from '@masschallenge/propellant-web';

export const Layout = ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => (
  <div data-propellant>
    <AppShell
      appearance="system"
      sidebar={
        <Sidebar label="Main" header={<Logo />}>
          <SidebarSection title="Program">
            <SidebarItem href="/overview" current>
              Overview
            </SidebarItem>
            <SidebarItem href="/startups">Startups</SidebarItem>
          </SidebarSection>
        </Sidebar>
      }
      toolbar={<Toolbar title="Overview" />}
    >
      {children}
    </AppShell>
  </div>
);
```

`SidebarItem` and `Button` render plain links by default. Pass your router's link component to
`linkAs` to keep client side navigation, where pages change without a full reload.

### 5. Choose light or dark

`AppShell` takes an `appearance` value:

| Value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Follows the light or dark setting of the operating system. |
| `light` | Always light. Use it while a product still has pages designed only for light. |
| `dark` | Always dark. |

Outside `AppShell`, set `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` on the boundary or any
element inside it.

## Websites

### With Tailwind CSS

Load the styles as in step 1. Then use tokens in arbitrary values (Tailwind classes with a value in
square brackets) and the text style utilities:

```html
<section data-propellant class="bg-[var(--bg-grouped)] px-[var(--page-margin)] py-12">
  <h1 class="text-large-title text-[var(--label)]">Programs</h1>
  <p class="text-body text-[var(--label-secondary)]">Find the program that fits your startup.</p>
</section>
```

Public pages may set their main headline in the brand display face:

```html
<h1 class="font-[family-name:var(--type-family-brand)] uppercase text-display">Apply now</h1>
```

### With your own CSS

Import the token stylesheet and use the CSS custom properties (the `var(--name)` values) directly:

```css
@import '@masschallenge/propellant-web/styles.scoped.css';

.card {
  background: var(--bg);
  border-radius: var(--corner-lg);
  padding: var(--space-6);
  color: var(--label);
  font-family: var(--type-family);
}
```

To apply the tokens to a whole site without a boundary element, import
`@masschallenge/propellant-web/styles.css` instead. It defines the same tokens on `:root`.

## Tokens

Use tokens by their role, never the raw values behind them:

| Kind | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Color | `--label`, `--label-secondary`, `--bg`, `--bg-grouped`, `--tint`, `--critical`, `--separator` |
| Type | `--type-family`, `--type-family-brand`, and the `text-body`, `text-headline` utilities |
| Shape | `--corner-sm`, `--corner-md`, `--corner-lg`, `--corner-xl`, `--corner-capsule` |
| Depth | `--shadow-float`, `--shadow-sheet`, `--material-bar` |
| Motion | `--spring-snappy`, `--spring-smooth`, `--ease-standard` |
| Layout | `--control-md`, `--row`, `--page-margin`, `--width-form`, `--space-4` |

The token reference on the documentation site lists every token with its light, dark, touch and
reduced motion values.

## What stays with you

Our components handle focus, keyboard support, contrast and announcements for screen readers. A
few things only your product can do:

- give every page one `h1` and a sensible heading order,
- write labels and button text that say what happens,
- give icon only buttons an accessible name,
- keep personal data out of analytics; fields mark their values private by default.

## Versioning

Propellant follows semantic versioning: the first number of a version changes only when an update
can break your code. Install a tagged version and read the changelog before moving to a new major
version.

# Using Propellant on websites

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/

You can give any website the MassChallenge look, whether it is built with WordPress, Squarespace,
Webflow, Wix, HubSpot or plain HTML. You do not need to be a developer.

The approach is the same everywhere:

1. **Set up the builder's own style settings first.** Every builder has a place to choose fonts,
   colors and button styles once for the whole site. Settings are easy for the next person to find
   and change, and they survive theme updates. For most sites, this is all you need.
2. **Add the logo** through the builder's logo setting.
3. **Use custom CSS only for what the settings cannot do**, such as the Oswald brand headline. Each
   guide gives you exact code to copy and paste, and keeps it as small as possible, because custom
   code is easy to forget and can break when a builder updates.

## Pick your builder

- [Squarespace](/web/websites/squarespace/)
- [WordPress](/web/websites/wordpress/)
- [Webflow](/web/websites/webflow/)
- [Wix](/web/websites/wix/)
- [HubSpot](/web/websites/hubspot/)
- [Plain HTML](/web/websites/html/)

Using something else? Read the [Squarespace guide](/web/websites/squarespace/) for the idea, then find
the same settings in your builder: almost every builder has a place for site fonts, site colors,
button styles and the logo.

## The website spec

Every guide sets these same values. Keep this page open while you work: each value is ready to
copy.

### Colors

| Use it for | Name | Hex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page background | White | `#FFFFFF` |
| Alternate section background | Mist | `#F3F6F7` |
| Body text and headings | Ink | `#1E282B` |
| Secondary text, such as captions | Slate | `#4B575B` |
| Links and buttons | Teal | `#065E6F` |
| Button hover, and dark brand sections | Deep teal | `#044451` |
| Accents on dark sections only | Bright teal | `#0FACBD` |
| Secondary buttons and tinted sections | Pale teal | `#D9F6FA` |
| Lines and dividers | Line | `#DBE1E3` |
| Highlights, always with Ink text | Yellow | `#FFC801` |
| Errors | Magenta | `#A30253` |

On Deep teal sections, use White text, White buttons with Deep teal text, and Bright teal for
accents. Never put Teal text on Deep teal.

### Fonts

| Font | Use it for | Where to get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lato | Everything except the big headline | Built into most builders, and on Google Fonts |
| Oswald | The big headline only, in capitals | Built into most builders, and on Google Fonts |

Propellant Sans, the font in our products, is our name for Lato 2.0, so Lato is the right choice
on websites.

### Text styles

Sizes are for desktop, with the mobile size in brackets. Line height is a multiple of the font
size; if your builder asks for a percentage, multiply by 100 (1.5 is 150%).

| Style | Font | Weight | Size | Line height | Letter spacing | Case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heading 1 (the big headline) | Oswald | 500 (Medium) | 64px (40px) | 1.0 | 1% (0.01em) | ALL CAPS |
| Heading 2 | Lato | 700 (Bold) | 40px (30px) | 1.15 | 0 | Sentence case |
| Heading 3 | Lato | 700 (Bold) | 30px (24px) | 1.2 | 0 | Sentence case |
| Heading 4 | Lato | 700 (Bold) | 24px (20px) | 1.25 | 0 | Sentence case |
| Paragraph large | Lato | 400 (Regular) | 20px (18px) | 1.5 | 0 | Sentence case |
| Paragraph | Lato | 400 (Regular) | 17px (16px) | 1.6 | 0 | Sentence case |
| Paragraph small | Lato | 400 (Regular) | 14px | 1.5 | 0 | Sentence case |
| Button | Lato | 700 (Bold) | 16px | 1.0 | 0 | Sentence case |

Only Heading 1 is in capitals. Everything else, buttons included, is sentence case: capital first
letter, the rest lower case except names.

### Buttons

| Button | Background | Text | Hover background | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primary | Teal `#065E6F` | White `#FFFFFF` | Deep teal `#044451` | Pill (fully rounded ends) |
| Secondary | Pale teal `#D9F6FA` | Teal `#065E6F` | `#C4EEF4` | Pill |
| On a Deep teal section | White `#FFFFFF` | Deep teal `#044451` | Pale teal `#D9F6FA` | Pill |

Padding: about 14px top and bottom, 28px left and right. No borders, no shadows, no capitals.

### Layout

- Keep paragraphs to about 720px wide, roughly 68 characters a line.
- Give sections about 96px of space above and below on desktop, 64px on mobile.
- Round images and cards by 12px. Buttons are pills.
- Use the logo files from the [brand guidelines](/brand/reference/), never a copy from somewhere else.

## The Propellant stylesheet

Some guides use a small stylesheet that loads the exact fonts and adds a few ready made classes,
such as `propellant-headline` and `propellant-button`. It only styles elements you add a class to,
so it never changes the rest of your site. Load it with this line, wherever a guide tells you to:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/dist/website.css"
/>
```

The `@v1.1.1` part pins your site to one release, so it never changes under you. A complete
example page is in [`examples/website.html`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web/blob/v1.1.1/examples/website.html).

| Class | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `propellant-headline` | Heading 1 from the spec: the big brand headline, in Oswald capitals. |
| `propellant-title-1`, `propellant-title-2`, `propellant-title-3` | Heading 2, Heading 3 and Heading 4 from the spec. |
| `propellant-body` | Paragraph from the spec. |
| `propellant-caption` | Paragraph small, in Slate, for dates and notes. |
| `propellant-text` | Body font and text color for a whole section. |
| `propellant-link` | A teal, underlined link. |
| `propellant-button` | The primary pill button. |
| `propellant-button propellant-button-secondary` | The secondary button. |
| `propellant-brand-band` | A Deep teal section with White text and buttons. |

## Keep it maintainable

- **Settings before code.** If something can be set in the builder's style settings, set it there.
- **Keep custom CSS short and labeled.** Paste only the snippets from these guides, and keep the
  comment line at the top of each so the next person knows where it came from.
- **Do not fight the theme.** If a theme setting and a snippet disagree, change the setting.
- **Check the published site and a phone.** Some code only runs on the published site, and every
  builder has a mobile view worth checking.

# Plain HTML

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/html/

If you write your own HTML pages, Propellant takes one line to set up. You will end up with our
fonts, colors, headings, buttons and brand sections on any page, in about ten minutes.

## Before you start

- A text editor and the HTML files for your site.
- The [website spec](/web/websites/) open in another tab.
- Somewhere to host the pages. Any static host works.

## Part 1: Load the stylesheet

Add this line inside the `<head>` of every page, before your own stylesheets:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/dist/website.css"
/>
```

That one file loads Lato (as Propellant Sans) and Oswald, defines every Propellant color and size,
and adds the class names below. It does not restyle anything you have not given a class to.

## Part 2: Use the classes

| Class | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `propellant-text` | Body font and text color. Put it on `<body>` so the whole page uses it. |
| `propellant-headline` | Heading 1: Oswald, in capitals. Use it once or twice per page. |
| `propellant-title-1`, `propellant-title-2`, `propellant-title-3` | Heading 2, Heading 3 and Heading 4. |
| `propellant-body` | Paragraph text. |
| `propellant-caption` | Small print, such as dates and notes. |
| `propellant-link` | A teal, underlined link. |
| `propellant-button` | The primary pill button. Works on `<a>` and `<button>`. |
| `propellant-button propellant-button-secondary` | The secondary button. |
| `propellant-brand-band` | A Deep teal section. Buttons and links inside it turn white. |

## Part 3: Build a page

Copy this into a new file named `index.html`, open it in a browser, and change the words:

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <title>Your page title</title>
    <link
      rel="stylesheet"
      href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/dist/website.css"
    />
    <style>
      body { margin: 0; }
      section { padding: 96px 24px; }
      .content { max-width: 720px; margin: 0 auto; display: grid; gap: 16px; }
      .actions { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px; }
      @media (max-width: 640px) { section { padding: 64px 24px; } }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body class="propellant-text">
    <section class="propellant-brand-band">
      <div class="content">
        <img
          src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png"
          alt="MassChallenge"
          height="32"
        />
        <h1 class="propellant-headline">Your big headline</h1>
        <p class="propellant-body">One or two sentences that say why this page matters.</p>
        <div class="actions">
          <a class="propellant-button" href="#">Your main action</a>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
    <section>
      <div class="content">
        <h2 class="propellant-title-1">A section heading</h2>
        <p class="propellant-body">
          Body text with a <a class="propellant-link" href="#">link</a>.
        </p>
        <div class="actions">
          <a class="propellant-button" href="#">Primary action</a>
          <a class="propellant-button propellant-button-secondary" href="#">Second choice</a>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  </body>
</html>
```

A similar finished page is in
[`examples/website.html`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web/blob/v1.1.1/examples/website.html).

## Part 4: Use the colors in your own CSS

Every color and size in the [website spec](/web/websites/) is also available by name, so your own
CSS stays in step with Propellant:

| Spec color | Use in CSS |
| --- | --- |
| Ink | `var(--label)` |
| Slate | `var(--label-secondary)` |
| Teal | `var(--tint)` |
| Deep teal | `var(--brand-surface)` |
| Mist | `var(--bg-grouped)` |
| White | `var(--bg)` |
| Line | `var(--separator)` |
| Yellow | `var(--highlight)` |

```css
.card {
  background: var(--bg);
  border: 1px solid var(--separator);
  border-radius: var(--corner-lg);
  padding: var(--space-6);
}
```

## Check your work

- The big headline is in Oswald capitals, and everything else is in Lato.
- Buttons are teal pills with white text and turn Deep teal on hover.
- Text on the Deep teal section is white, and its button is white with Deep teal text.
- The page reads well on a phone.

## If something looks off

- **Fonts did not change.** Check that the link is inside `<head>` and the address ends in
  `dist/website.css`. Open the address in a browser: you should see CSS, not an error.
- **A button looks like a plain link.** Check the class is spelled `propellant-button`.
- **Your own CSS is ignored.** Load your stylesheet after the Propellant link, so yours comes last.

# HubSpot

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/hubspot/

This guide takes a HubSpot website or landing page (Content Hub) from its default look to the
MassChallenge look: Lato and Oswald type, the teal palette, pill buttons, and White, Mist and Deep
teal sections. Almost all of it happens in HubSpot's theme settings, with no code. Plan on about an
hour for the settings and logo, and a little longer if you also build a sample page.

We wrote the steps for Elevate, HubSpot's current default theme, because most new HubSpot sites
start on it. If your site uses another theme, the same ideas apply, but the setting names will
differ: a theme only shows the settings its developer built in.

## Before you start

**Your plan.** Theme settings, the brand kit, the drag and drop editor and the mobile view are
available on every HubSpot plan, including the free tools. Custom code is different:

| What | Where it lives | Which plans |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theme settings, brand kit, section styles | The page editor and Marketing, then Brand | All plans |
| Site header HTML (code added to every page) | Settings, Content, Pages | Varies by plan. HubSpot says not every account can edit it. Check your account. |
| A child theme with its own CSS file | Design Manager | All plans. Free tools and Content Hub Starter allow one child theme, Professional five, Enterprise ten. |
| Attaching a stylesheet to a page or a whole domain | Page settings, or Settings, Content, Pages | Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise, and not for most theme templates (see Part 4) |

**Your permissions.** To change the brand kit you need to be a Super Admin or have the Edit account
defaults permission. To change site wide code you need the Website settings permission.

**Keep the spec open.** Every value in this guide comes from the
[website spec](/web/websites/). Keep it open in another tab so you can copy hex codes from it.

**Download the logo files.** Save these from our logo folder to your computer:

- https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png
  (the main logo, for White and Mist backgrounds)
- https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png
  (for Deep teal backgrounds)
- https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png
  (the MC monogram, for the site icon)

The monogram also comes in `-white` and `-black` versions. Read the
[logo rules](/brand/reference/#logo) before you place it: never stretch, recolor or redraw it.

## How HubSpot's style settings fit together

HubSpot has two places for your look, and it helps to know what each one does.

- **The brand kit** (Marketing, then Brand) holds your logo, site icon, brand colors and brand
  fonts. HubSpot uses these across its tools: the logo fills the header, and the colors show up as
  swatches in every color picker.
- **Theme settings** decide how your pages actually look: the fonts for each heading, the colors of
  each section type, and the shape and colors of each button. A change here updates every page that
  uses the theme.

**Which one wins.** Your theme settings decide what visitors see. A theme can use the brand kit
values as its starting point, but once you set a value in theme settings, that value is what the
page shows. Elevate's colors and fonts do not follow the brand kit at all, so set them in both
places: the brand kit for the swatches and the logo, theme settings for the pages. And if one page
looks different from the rest, check that page's own styles, because a style set on a single page
or module beats the theme.

**How Elevate handles color.** Elevate has six palette colors (three base colors and three accent
colors) and four section types: Light section 1, Light section 2, Light section 3 and Dark section 1.
Each section type has its own background, text, caption and link colors. Modules such as Heading
then have a Text color option that picks which section type's colors to use.

## Part 1: Set up site styles (no code)

### Step 1: Fill in the brand kit

1. Click **More** in the top bar, then go to **Marketing**, then **Brand**. (If you do not see
   More, go straight to Marketing, then Brand.)
2. Stay on the **Brand Kit** tab.
3. Under brand colors, click **Edit Colors** and enter these hex codes in each box:

   | Brand kit slot | Spec color | Hex |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Primary | Teal | `#065E6F` |
   | Secondary | Deep teal | `#044451` |
   | Accent 1 | Bright teal | `#0FACBD` |
   | Accent 2 | Pale teal | `#D9F6FA` |
   | Accent 3 | Mist | `#F3F6F7` |
   | Additional | Ink | `#1E282B` |
   | Additional | Slate | `#4B575B` |
   | Additional | Line | `#DBE1E3` |
   | Additional | Yellow | `#FFC801` |
   | Additional | Magenta | `#A30253` |

   Click **Add** to make each additional color. Click **Save**.

4. In the **Fonts** section, click **Edit** next to each font and pick **Lato** for the main or
   body font and **Oswald** for the heading or display font, then save. Your account may label
   these two fonts differently; the rule is Lato for everything, Oswald for the big headline only.
5. Leave this tab open. You will add the logo here in Part 2.

### Step 2: Open the theme settings

You can reach theme settings from any page that uses your theme.

1. Go to **Content**, then **Website Pages** (or **Landing Pages**), and click the name of any
   page to open the editor.
2. Open the theme settings in one of two ways:
   - Click the **Global theme styles** icon in the left sidebar (pages only), or
   - Click the **Edit** menu in the toolbar and choose **Theme**.
3. You will see groups you can expand. In Elevate they are under **Foundation** (Fonts and Colors)
   and **Elements** (Buttons, Links, Forms, Cards and Tags).

You can also get here from the brand kit: next to your active theme, click **Edit / Preview**.

Nothing goes live until you click **Publish theme** (or **Publish** in the universal editor), and
publishing updates every page that uses the theme.

### Step 3: Set the palette colors

Open **Foundation**, then **Colors**. Enter these:

| Elevate setting | Spec color | Hex | What Elevate uses it for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base color 1 | White | `#FFFFFF` | Page background (Light section 1) |
| Base color 2 | Mist | `#F3F6F7` | Alternate background (Light section 2) |
| Base color 3 | Ink | `#1E282B` | Text and headings |
| Accent color 1 | Pale teal | `#D9F6FA` | Tinted background (Light section 3) |
| Accent color 2 | Bright teal | `#0FACBD` | Accents on dark sections |
| Accent color 3 | Teal | `#065E6F` | Buttons and links |

### Step 4: Set the section colors

Still in **Colors**, open **More settings**, then **Sections**. Use **Choose section to edit** to
switch between the four section types, and enter these values for each:

| Setting | Light section 1 | Light section 2 | Light section 3 | Dark section 1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Section background color | White `#FFFFFF` | Mist `#F3F6F7` | Pale teal `#D9F6FA` | Deep teal `#044451` |
| Default text color | Ink `#1E282B` | Ink `#1E282B` | Ink `#1E282B` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Accent text color | Teal `#065E6F` | Teal `#065E6F` | Teal `#065E6F` | Bright teal `#0FACBD` |
| Caption text color | Slate `#4B575B` | Slate `#4B575B` | Slate `#4B575B` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Link colors | Primary | Primary | Primary | Secondary |

Elevate's Dark section 1 starts out using Base color 3 (now Ink) as its background, so change its
background to Deep teal here. Never put Teal text on Deep teal.

### Step 5: Set the fonts and text styles

Open **Foundation**, then **Fonts**.

1. Set **Base font** to **Lato**. Every heading and paragraph starts from this font.
2. Open **Font elements**, then **Headings** and **Body**, and set each style:

   | Elevate setting | Spec style | Font | Weight | Size |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | Heading 1 (H1) | Heading 1 | Oswald | 500 (Medium) | 64px |
   | Heading 2 (H2) | Heading 2 | Lato | 700 (Bold) | 40px |
   | Heading 3 (H3) | Heading 3 | Lato | 700 (Bold) | 30px |
   | Heading 4 (H4) | Heading 4 | Lato | 700 (Bold) | 24px |
   | Paragraph | Paragraph | Lato | 400 (Regular) | 17px |

3. Under **Other elements**, open **Caption** and set it to Lato, 400 (Regular), 14px, and set
   **Case** to **None** (Elevate's captions start in capitals, and the spec keeps them in sentence
   case).
4. Leave Heading 5, Heading 6 and Block quote alone. The spec does not use them.

Elevate's font settings have no line height, letter spacing or capitals option for headings.
Headings get a line height of 1.2 and paragraphs 1.55, which is close to the spec. The one thing
you will notice is Heading 1: to show it in capitals, you can either type the headline in capitals
or add the small snippet in Part 4. We recommend the snippet: you keep typing headlines in
sentence case, and the capitals come from the style, which is how the brand works everywhere else.

### Step 6: Set the buttons

Open **Elements**, then **Buttons**. Elevate has four button styles. Use three of them:

| Setting | Primary button | Secondary button | Accent button (for Deep teal sections) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Background | Filled | Filled | Filled |
| Shape | pill | pill | pill |
| Border | 0px | 0px | 0px |
| Default state: Fill color | Teal `#065E6F` | Pale teal `#D9F6FA` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Default state: Border color | Teal `#065E6F` | Pale teal `#D9F6FA` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Default state: Text color | White `#FFFFFF` | Teal `#065E6F` | Deep teal `#044451` |
| Hover state: Fill color | Deep teal `#044451` | `#C4EEF4` | Pale teal `#D9F6FA` |
| Hover state: Border color | Deep teal `#044451` | `#C4EEF4` | Pale teal `#D9F6FA` |
| Hover state: Text color | White `#FFFFFF` | Teal `#065E6F` | Deep teal `#044451` |
| Text: Font | Lato, 700 (Bold), 16px | Lato, 700 (Bold), 16px | Lato, 700 (Bold), 16px |

Notes:

- The border color matches the fill so the button looks borderless even if someone later adds a
  border width.
- Elevate's primary button text starts out using Base color 2, which is now Mist, so set it to
  White explicitly.
- Leave the **Tertiary button** unused. If you want it tidy, give it the same values as the
  Secondary button.
- Elevate has no separate corner radius number: **pill** gives fully rounded ends, which is what
  the spec asks for. Other themes may show a **Corner radius** field instead; set it to a large
  number such as 100px for a pill.
- When you add a button to a page, pick **Medium** for **Button size**. Elevate does not show the
  exact padding, so compare it by eye with the spec (about 14px top and bottom, 28px left and
  right).

Type every button label in sentence case, such as Apply now. The spec has no capitals on buttons.

### Step 7: Set links, forms and cards

1. **Links, Primary links.** Default state: Text color Teal `#065E6F`, turn on **Show underline**,
   Underline color Teal `#065E6F`. Hover state: Text color Deep teal `#044451`, Show underline on,
   Underline color Deep teal `#044451`.
2. **Links, Secondary links** (used on Deep teal sections). Default state: Text color White
   `#FFFFFF`, Show underline on, Underline color Bright teal `#0FACBD`. Hover state: Text color
   White `#FFFFFF`, Show underline on, Underline color White `#FFFFFF`.
3. **Forms.** Set the field border color and the form border color to Line `#DBE1E3`, and the
   label text color and input text color to Ink `#1E282B`.
4. **Cards.** For each card variant you use, set **Card shape** to **Rounded** and the border
   color to Line `#DBE1E3`. Elevate's rounded corners are not a number you can type, so they may
   not be exactly the spec's 12px. That is fine.
5. Click **Publish theme**.

### Step 8: Check the mobile sizes

HubSpot's editor has a desktop icon and a mobile icon at the top of the screen. Click the mobile
icon to see the phone layout.

Elevate does not have separate mobile font settings. On screens narrower than about 767px it
shrinks every heading to 80% of its desktop size automatically:

| Style | Desktop (you set) | Elevate on phones | Spec on phones |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | 64px | about 51px | 40px |
| Heading 2 | 40px | 32px | 30px |
| Heading 3 | 30px | 24px | 24px |
| Heading 4 | 24px | about 19px | 20px |
| Paragraph | 17px | 17px | 16px |

Heading 3 is exact and the others are close. If you want the phone sizes to match the spec
exactly, the Part 4 snippet does it. The biggest gap is Heading 1, which can wrap awkwardly on a
phone at 51px.

## Part 2: Add the logo and site icon

### The logo

1. Go back to **Marketing**, then **Brand**, **Brand Kit** tab.
2. Click **Add logo +**, then **Upload**, and choose `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png`.
3. Enter **MassChallenge** as the **Logo name** and **MassChallenge** as the **Logo alt text**
   (the words screen readers say and search engines read).
4. In **Link**, enter your home page address so the logo takes people home.
5. Choose **Yes** to make it the default logo, and click **Save**.

Elevate's site header uses the brand kit logo by default. To check, open any page, click the site
header, and look at its **Logo** field. If your header has a Deep teal background, change that one
header's logo to `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png`.

Keep the logo at least 24px tall, and leave clear space around it of half its height. If the header
is so small that the horizontal logo would drop below 24px, use the monogram instead.

### The site icon (favicon)

The favicon is the small icon in the browser tab.

1. In the same **Brand Kit** tab, click **Add Favicon +**.
2. Upload `masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png`.
3. Name it **MassChallenge monogram**, choose **Yes** to make it the default, and click **Save**.

The favicon only applies to pages hosted on HubSpot.

## Part 3: Build on brand pages

Everything below uses the drag and drop editor. Each page is made of **sections**, which hold
**rows**, which hold **columns** of **modules** (Heading, Rich text, Button, Image and so on).

### Make a White, Mist or Deep teal section

1. In the page editor, click the section you want to style. (Hover over the section and click its
   edge, or click its name in the **Contents** tab of the left sidebar.)
2. Open the **Styles** tab in the sidebar.
3. Under **Background**, choose **Color** and enter the hex code:
   - White section: `#FFFFFF`
   - Mist section: `#F3F6F7`
   - Deep teal section: `#044451`
4. Under **Alignment and spacing**, set the top and bottom padding to **96px**.
5. Click the **mobile** icon at the top of the editor, select the same section, and set the top and
   bottom padding to **64px**. Changes you make in the mobile view only apply to phones.

Rows and columns have their own background settings too. Keep backgrounds on the section, so the
whole band changes color edge to edge.

**Text inside a Deep teal section.** For each Heading or Rich text module in the section, open its
**Styles** tab and set **Text color** to **Dark section text color**. That gives you White text,
Bright teal accents and the White secondary links you set in Part 1. On White and Mist sections,
leave it on **Light section 1 text color** (or Light section 2).

Alternate White and Mist sections down the page, and save Deep teal for one or two strong moments,
such as the opening band or a final call to action.

### Add the Heading 1 headline

1. Drag a **Heading** module into the top section.
2. Type the headline in sentence case, for example: Build what comes next.
3. Set **Semantic heading level** to **Heading 1**. This tells search engines and screen readers it
   is the main headline.
4. In the **Styles** tab, set **Heading style** to **Heading 1**.

Use one Heading 1 per page. Use Heading 2 for each section title below it.

### Add buttons

1. Drag a **Button** module into a column.
2. Enter the **Button text** in sentence case and choose the **Link**.
3. In the **Styles** tab, set **Button style**:
   - **Primary** for the main action on a White or Mist section.
   - **Secondary** for a second, quieter action next to it.
   - **Accent** for any button on a Deep teal section (White with Deep teal text).
4. Set **Button size** to **Medium**.

### Build a sample home page

1. **Opening band.** A Deep teal section. Add a Heading module (Heading 1, Dark section text color)
   and a Rich text paragraph below it, also on Dark section text color. Add a Button module with
   the Accent style.
2. **What we do.** A White section. A Heading 2, a paragraph of no more than about 720px wide (set
   the column narrower, or use a two column row and leave one empty), and a Primary button.
3. **Three cards.** A Mist section with a row of three columns, each with an image, a Heading 3 and
   a short paragraph.
4. **Final call to action.** A White section with a Heading 2, a Primary button and a Secondary
   button side by side.
5. Click the mobile icon and check each section before you publish.

## Part 4: Custom CSS (optional, only what settings cannot do)

You can stop at Part 3. Add code only if you want these four things, which Elevate's settings
cannot do:

- **Heading 1 in capitals** with 1% letter spacing and a line height of 1.0. Elevate has no case,
  letter spacing or line height setting for headings.
- **Exact phone sizes** for Heading 1, Heading 2, Heading 4 and paragraphs. Elevate only shrinks
  headings by a fixed 80%.
- **Exact line heights** for Heading 2 (1.15), Heading 4 (1.25) and paragraphs (1.6).

The snippet targets Elevate's own heading tags and its `hs-elevate-h1` style names, so it only
touches headings and body text.

### Option A: Site header HTML (simplest)

This adds the code to the top of every page on a domain. Whether your plan includes it varies, so
look for the field in your account.

1. Click the **settings** icon (the gear) in the top bar.
2. In the left sidebar, go to **Content**, then **Pages**.
3. In **Choose a domain to edit its settings**, pick your website's domain, or **Default settings
   for all domains**.
4. Find **Site header HTML**. (In some accounts it sits on a tab called **Templates**.) If you
   picked one domain and the field is locked, click **Override default settings**.
5. Paste this at the end of whatever is already in the field:

   ```html
   <style>
     /* Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web */
     body h1,
     body .hs-elevate-h1 {
       text-transform: uppercase;
       letter-spacing: 0.01em;
       line-height: 1;
     }
     body h2,
     body .hs-elevate-h2 {
       line-height: 1.15;
     }
     body h4,
     body .hs-elevate-h4 {
       line-height: 1.25;
     }
     html body {
       line-height: 1.6;
     }
     @media (max-width: 766px) {
       body h1,
       body .hs-elevate-h1 {
         font-size: 40px;
       }
       body h2,
       body .hs-elevate-h2 {
         font-size: 30px;
       }
       body h4,
       body .hs-elevate-h4 {
         font-size: 20px;
       }
       html body {
         font-size: 16px;
       }
     }
   </style>
   ```

6. Click **Save** in the bottom left.

To see a single page with the code before you add it everywhere, open that page, go to the
**Settings** menu, then **Advanced**, and paste it into **Head HTML** under **Additional code
snippets** instead.

**To remove it later**, open the same field and delete everything from `<style>` to `</style>`,
then save. Leave any other code in the field alone (it is often tracking code someone else added).

### Option B: A child theme

A child theme is a copy of Elevate that keeps getting Elevate's updates, plus an empty CSS file of
its own. Use this if your plan does not include Site header HTML, or if you prefer to keep styles
with the theme.

1. Go to **Content**, then **Design Manager**.
2. Open the **@hubspot** folder, right click the **elevate** folder and choose **Create child
   theme**. (Elevate itself cannot be cloned, so a child theme is the way to change it.)
3. Give it a name, such as MassChallenge, and click **Create child theme**.
4. Open the new theme's CSS file (named `child.css` unless you renamed it) and paste the snippet
   from Option A **without** the `<style>` and `</style>` lines. Click **Publish changes**.
5. Build new pages with the child theme's templates. Existing pages keep their old theme until you
   swap each page's template to the matching child theme template.
6. Open theme settings on a child theme page and check your Part 1 values. The child theme starts
   from Elevate's settings, so you may need to enter them again there.

**To remove it later**, delete the snippet from the CSS file and click **Publish changes**.

### Option C: Attached stylesheets (usually not for Elevate)

HubSpot can also attach a CSS file from the Design Manager to one page (page **Settings**, then
**Advanced**, then **Stylesheets**) or to a whole domain (**Settings**, **Content**, **Pages**,
**CSS & Stylesheets**). Both need Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise, and neither works on
Elevate's templates: page stylesheets are not available for theme templates, and domain stylesheets
only work on theme templates built to accept them. Use Option A or B instead.

### Using the Propellant stylesheet instead

The [Propellant stylesheet](/web/websites/#the-propellant-stylesheet) loads Lato and Oswald and
adds ready made classes that match the spec: `propellant-headline` is Heading 1 (including the
capitals and the 40px phone size), `propellant-title-1`, `propellant-title-2` and
`propellant-title-3` are Heading 2, 3 and 4, `propellant-body` is Paragraph, and
`propellant-caption` is Paragraph small in Slate. To load it, paste this line into Site header
HTML (Option A) on its own, outside any `<style>` tags:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/dist/website.css"
/>
```

It only styles elements you give a class to, so it changes nothing on its own. In HubSpot you add a
class by editing the HTML of a Rich text module (its source code view), for example:

```html
<h1 class="propellant-headline">Build what comes next</h1>
```

For most HubSpot sites the theme settings plus the Option A snippet are simpler, because you
keep editing in HubSpot's own modules. For buttons, keep using the Button module with the styles
from Part 1: Elevate styles every plain link on the page, and its link color rule can win over
a `propellant-button` class placed inside a Rich text module. To remove the stylesheet, delete the
`<link ... />` line.

## Check your work

On desktop:

- [ ] Headings and paragraphs are in Lato; only the big Heading 1 is in Oswald.
- [ ] Heading 1 shows in capitals (with the snippet) and every other heading is in sentence case.
- [ ] Body text is Ink, captions are Slate, and links are Teal and underlined.
- [ ] Primary buttons are Teal pills with White text that turn Deep teal on hover.
- [ ] Secondary buttons are Pale teal pills with Teal text.
- [ ] Deep teal sections have White text, White buttons with Deep teal text, and no Teal text.
- [ ] The full color logo sits in the header and links home; the favicon shows the monogram.

On a phone (use the editor's mobile icon, then check the published page on a real phone):

- [ ] Heading 1 fits without awkward wrapping.
- [ ] Sections have about 64px of space above and below.
- [ ] Buttons are easy to tap and their labels fit on one line.

## If something looks off

- **One page ignores the theme.** That page or module has its own style set. Select the module or
  section, open its **Styles** tab, and clear the override (for example set Background back to
  **None**).
- **Headings are still in the old font.** You changed the brand kit but not the theme. Set the fonts
  in theme settings (Part 1, Step 5) and click **Publish theme**.
- **Text on a Deep teal section is hard to read.** The module is still on a light text color. Set
