  its **Text color** to **Dark section text color**.
- **Primary button text is pale gray instead of White.** Set **Primary button**, **Default state**,
  **Text color** to `#FFFFFF`; Elevate starts it on Base color 2.
- **The snippet does nothing.** Check that you saved the domain you are viewing (or Default
  settings for all domains), that the code sits between `<style>` and `</style>`, and look at the
  published page rather than the editor preview.
- **A theme update changed something.** Open theme settings and compare each value with the
  [spec](/web/websites/). Settings are the source of truth; change them there rather than adding
  more code.

# Squarespace

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/squarespace/

This guide takes a Squarespace 7.1 site, new or existing, and gives it the MassChallenge look:
Lato text, the Oswald headline in capitals, the teal palette, pill shaped buttons and sections in
White, Mist and Deep teal. Most of it is point and click in Squarespace's own style settings. One
optional step adds a few lines of code for the headline. Plan on about an hour the first time,
and less once you know where things live.

All of the steps are for Squarespace version 7.1, the current version. If your site is on version
7.0, the menus are different and this guide will not match. To check, open the **Pages** panel
and look at the bottom: Squarespace shows your site's version there.

## Before you start

**Your plan.** Most of this guide works on every Squarespace plan. The code steps depend on your
plan:

| What | Where it lives | Plans that allow it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Custom CSS (small pieces of style code) | Pages panel, **Custom Code**, **Custom CSS** | All plans |
| Code injection (code added to the head of every page) | Pages panel, **Custom Code**, **Code Injection** | Core, Plus, Advanced and some older (legacy) plans |

You only need Custom CSS for this guide, so any plan will do. Code injection is an alternative for
one step, and it is only on Core and above.

**Keep the spec open.** Every value you will type comes from the [website spec](/web/websites/).
Keep it open in another tab so you can copy hex codes from it.

**Download the logo files.** Use these files only, never a copy from somewhere else. Open each link
and save the image to your computer:

- Full color horizontal logo, for the header on White:
  https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png
- White horizontal logo, for Deep teal backgrounds:
  https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png
- Full color monogram (the MC mark on its own), for the browser icon:
  https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png
- There are also `-white` and `-black` versions of the monogram, and a `-black` horizontal logo,
  at the same address with the color word changed. The [brand guidelines](/brand/reference/) say when to
  use each one.

**One habit that saves trouble.** In Squarespace, style settings apply to the whole site. If you
change a font size or color with the text toolbar inside a single block, that block stops
following the site settings. Set things once in Site styles and leave the toolbar for choosing a
format such as Heading 2.

## Part 1: Set up site styles (no code)

This is the main part of the guide. You will set fonts, colors and buttons once, and every page
picks them up.

### Open Site styles

1. Open the **Pages** panel and click any page.
2. Click the **paintbrush** icon in the top right corner. The **Site styles** panel opens.
3. You will see sections such as **Fonts**, **Colors**, **Buttons** and **Spacing**. Click the
   **>** arrow next to a section to open its settings.

Two warnings before you start:

- Site styles has a **Themes** option, and Fonts and Buttons each offer ready made **packs**.
  Picking a theme or a pack replaces your fonts, colors or buttons in one go. Once you have set
  things up, do not click a different theme or pack. If you do by accident, use the **undo** arrow
  at the top of the panel.
- Click **Save** at the top of the editor when you finish each section, so nothing is lost.

### Step 1: Fonts

How Squarespace fonts work, in plain words: text comes in four groups, **Headings**,
**Paragraphs**, **Buttons** and **Miscellaneous** (small extras such as dates and captions). Each
group has one font for the whole group. Inside Headings there are four sizes, Heading 1 to Heading
4. Inside Paragraphs there are three sizes, Paragraph 1 (large), Paragraph 2 (normal) and
Paragraph 3 (small). Sizes are set in **rem**, which means "times the base size". With a base size
of 16, 2rem is 32 pixels.

That one font per group is the only real limit. All four heading sizes share one font and one
capitals setting, so Squarespace cannot set Heading 1 in Oswald capitals and Headings 2 to 4 in
Lato on its own. You will set every heading to Lato here, and Part 4 adds a few lines of code that
turn Heading 1 into the Oswald headline. If you skip Part 4, Heading 1 stays a large, bold Lato
heading, which still looks tidy and on brand.

**Choose a starting font pack**

1. In Site styles, click **Fonts**.
2. If you want, click **>** next to Fonts, then **All Font Packs**, then **Sans-serif**, and pick
   any pack. It does not matter which: you are about to change every font in it. If your site
   already has a pack, skip this.

**Set the base size**

1. Click **>** next to **Fonts**.
2. Use the **+** and **-** buttons to set the **Base size** to **16**. Every size below assumes a
   base of 16.

**Headings**

Click **Headings** and set:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Font | **Lato** (type "Lato" in the font search) |
| Style or weight | **700** (Bold) |
| Line height | **1.2em** (see the note below) |
| Letter spacing | **0em** |
| Text transform | **None** |

Then set each size:

| Squarespace size | Spec style | Desktop size in the spec | Enter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | Heading 1 (the big headline) | 64px | **4rem** |
| Heading 2 | Heading 2 | 40px | **2.5rem** |
| Heading 3 | Heading 3 | 30px | **1.875rem** |
| Heading 4 | Heading 4 | 24px | **1.5rem** |

A note on line height: the spec gives each heading its own line height (1.0, 1.15, 1.2 and 1.25).
If your panel shows a line height for each heading size, enter those values in em (1.0em, 1.15em,
1.2em, 1.25em). If it shows one line height for all headings, use 1.2em, which sits in the middle
and looks right for Headings 2 to 4. Part 4 sets Heading 1 to 1.0.

If a slider will not land on an exact value, click the number and type it.

**Paragraphs**

Click **Paragraphs** and set:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Font | **Lato** |
| Style or weight | **400** (Regular) |
| Line height | **1.6em** (see the note below) |
| Letter spacing | **0em** |
| Text transform | **None** |

Then set each size:

| Squarespace size | Spec style | Desktop size in the spec | Enter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Paragraph 1 | Paragraph large | 20px | **1.25rem** |
| Paragraph 2 | Paragraph | 17px | **1.0625rem** |
| Paragraph 3 | Paragraph small | 14px | **0.875rem** |

If your panel offers a line height for each paragraph size, use 1.5em for Paragraph 1, 1.6em for
Paragraph 2 and 1.5em for Paragraph 3. If there is one value for all, use 1.6em.

**Buttons**

Click **Buttons** (inside Fonts) and set:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Font | **Lato** |
| Style or weight | **700** (Bold) |
| Size | **1rem** (16px) |
| Letter spacing | **0em** |
| Text transform | **None** |

Buttons are in sentence case, never capitals, so make sure Text transform is **None**. If your
panel shows separate font settings for Primary, Secondary and Tertiary buttons, set all three the
same way.

**Miscellaneous**

Click **Miscellaneous** and set the font to **Lato**, weight **400**, letter spacing **0em** and
text transform **None**. This covers small text such as dates, so it should match your paragraphs.

**If Lato is not in the list**

Squarespace's library holds hundreds of Google Fonts but not every one. Lato should be there; if
your search finds nothing, you can upload it:

1. Download Lato from Google Fonts (fonts.google.com, search "Lato"). You need the Regular (400)
   and Bold (700) files.
2. In Site styles, click **>** next to Fonts, then click **Headings** (or Paragraphs).
3. Click the font dropdown, then click the **upload** icon.
4. Drag in one font file, or click **+** and choose it. Upload each weight as its own file.
   Squarespace accepts .otf, .ttf, .woff and .woff2 files.
5. Your fonts appear under **Uploaded** in every font dropdown. Choose Lato there.

You do not need to do this for Oswald. Part 4 loads Oswald for you.

### Step 2: Colors

How Squarespace colors work, in plain words: there are two layers.

1. **The palette.** Every site has a palette of exactly five colors. They are the starting point
   for everything else.
2. **Color themes.** Squarespace builds ten color themes from the palette. A color theme is a full
   set of colors for one section: its background, headings, paragraphs, links and buttons. You
   give each section of a page one theme. The ten themes are named from lightest to darkest:
   **Lightest 1**, **Lightest 2**, **Light 1**, **Light 2**, **Bright 1**, **Bright 2**,
   **Dark 1**, **Dark 2**, **Darkest 1** and **Darkest 2**.

Inside a theme you can pick any color for any part, either one of the five palette colors or a
**Custom** color you type in. That is how you get colors such as Pale teal, which do not fit in a
five color palette.

We use three themes, one for each kind of section in the spec:

| Section in the spec | Squarespace theme |
| --- | --- |
| White (the normal page background) | **Lightest 1** |
| Mist (the alternate section background) | **Light 1** |
| Deep teal (the dark brand section) | **Darkest 1** |

**Edit the palette**

1. In Site styles, click **>** next to **Colors**.
2. Click **Edit palette**.
3. Click each of the five colors in turn and type its hex code into the value field, so the palette
   matches this table from lightest to darkest:

| Palette position | Spec color | Hex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (lightest) | White | `#FFFFFF` |
| 2 | Mist | `#F3F6F7` |
| 3 | Teal | `#065E6F` |
| 4 | Deep teal | `#044451` |
| 5 (darkest) | Ink | `#1E282B` |

4. Click **Save**.

Changing the palette can change your color themes too, so always edit the palette first and the
themes second. If you edit the palette again later, check your three themes afterwards.

**Edit the three color themes**

For each of the three themes below:

1. In the Colors panel, click the theme (for example **Lightest 1**).
2. Click a part, such as **Background**. Pick from the **Palette** tab, or click **Custom** and type
   the hex code.
3. Work through every part in the table.
4. Click **Save**.

The exact names of the parts can differ slightly from site to site. Squarespace calls the four
heading sizes Heading (Extra Large), Heading (Large), Heading (Medium) and Heading (Small): they
are Heading 1 to Heading 4. Paragraphs are Paragraph (Large), Paragraph (Medium) and Paragraph
(Small). If you see a part that is not in this table, such as a block's own colors, match it to the
closest row.

| Part | Lightest 1 (White) | Light 1 (Mist) | Darkest 1 (Deep teal) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Background | White `#FFFFFF` | Mist `#F3F6F7` | Deep teal `#044451` |
| All four headings | Ink `#1E282B` | Ink `#1E282B` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Paragraph (Large) and (Medium) | Ink `#1E282B` | Ink `#1E282B` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Paragraph (Small) | Slate `#4B575B` | Slate `#4B575B` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Links (paragraph and heading links) | Teal `#065E6F` | Teal `#065E6F` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Primary button background | Teal `#065E6F` | Teal `#065E6F` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Primary button text | White `#FFFFFF` | White `#FFFFFF` | Deep teal `#044451` |
| Secondary button background | Pale teal `#D9F6FA` | Pale teal `#D9F6FA` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Secondary button text | Teal `#065E6F` | Teal `#065E6F` | Deep teal `#044451` |
| Tertiary button background | Pale teal `#D9F6FA` | Pale teal `#D9F6FA` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Tertiary button text | Teal `#065E6F` | Teal `#065E6F` | Deep teal `#044451` |
| Lines and dividers | Line `#DBE1E3` | Line `#DBE1E3` | Bright teal `#0FACBD` |
| Site title and navigation links (if listed) | Ink `#1E282B` | Ink `#1E282B` | White `#FFFFFF` |

Why the buttons look like this: on Deep teal the spec allows only White buttons with Deep teal
text, so every button type in that theme is set the same way. Squarespace only uses Tertiary
buttons in a few places, such as the cookie banner, so we make them match Secondary.

Never put Teal text on Deep teal. If you see Teal anywhere in the Darkest 1 column on your screen,
change it to White.

You can leave the other seven themes alone. Just use only these three for your sections. Yellow and
Magenta from the spec are not set here: Yellow is for occasional highlights (always with Ink text)
and Magenta is for errors.

### Step 3: Buttons

How Squarespace buttons work, in plain words: there are three button types, **Primary**,
**Secondary** and **Tertiary**. Each has its own shape, outline and padding (the space between the
text and the edge of the button). Colors do not live here: they come from the color theme of the
section, which you set in Step 2.

Most buttons on a Squarespace site are Primary. Button blocks, header buttons and form submit
buttons can be switched to Secondary or Tertiary.

1. In Site styles, click **>** next to **Buttons**.
2. Click **Primary** and set:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Fill | **Fill** (a solid background, sometimes called Solid). Not No Fill. |
| Shape | **Pill** (fully rounded ends) |
| Outline | Slide to **0** (no border) |
| Padding | Click **...** and set **Top & Bottom** to **14px** and **Left & Right** to **28px** |

3. Click **Font** if you did not set button fonts in Step 1: Lato, 700, 1rem, letter spacing 0em,
   text transform None.
4. Click **Apply to all Button Types**, so Secondary and Tertiary get the same shape and padding.
5. Click **Save**.

If the padding field does not accept pixels, choose **M** and compare the button with the spec:
it should be a little under three times as wide as it is tall for a short label such as "Apply".

If you see shadow or raised options, turn them off. The spec has no borders and no shadows.

Hover color: Squarespace has no setting for the color a button turns when you point at it. It
fades the button slightly instead. The spec asks for a set hover color (Deep teal for primary).
Part 4 has a small snippet for that. It is optional: a faded hover still works.

### Step 4: Spacing

The spec asks for about 96px of space above and below each section on desktop and 64px on phones,
and for paragraphs about 720px wide.

1. In Site styles, click **Spacing**. You can leave **Site Margin** (the space between your content
   and the edge of the screen) at its default.
2. Section spacing is set on each section, not here. See "Section spacing" in Part 3.

### Step 5: Mobile

Squarespace 7.1 always rearranges and resizes your site for phones, and you cannot turn that off.
There is no separate set of mobile font sizes in Site styles: headings shrink on their own as the
screen gets narrower. The spec's mobile sizes (for example 40px for Heading 1) are close to what
Squarespace does by itself. If your Heading 1 is too big or too small on a phone, Part 4 has a
snippet that sets it to exactly 40px.

To see your phone layout, switch the editor to its mobile view (the phone icon at the top of the
page editor). In Fluid Engine sections (Squarespace's drag and drop grid), you can move and resize
blocks for mobile separately from desktop. Always check every page there before you publish.

## Part 2: Add the logo and site icon

### The logo

1. Click **Edit** in the top left corner of the page.
2. Hover over the header (the strip at the top with your site name) and click **Edit Site Header**.
3. Click the site title or logo, then click the **pencil** icon.
4. In **Logo Image**, click **+**, then **Upload File**, and choose
   `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png`.
5. Use the slider to set the logo height. Keep it at **24px or taller**, because below 24px the
   wordmark stops being readable. A height around 32px works well in most headers.
6. In **Mobile Logo Image**, upload the same file and use **Mobile Logo Max Height** to keep it at
   least 24px tall.
7. Click **Save**.

Keep the header on a White background so the full color logo fits. In **Edit Site Header**, click
**Colors** and choose **Lightest 1**. If you ever give the header a Deep teal background, upload
`masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png` instead: never put the full color logo on Deep teal.

Logo rules from the [brand guidelines](/brand/reference/):

- Keep clear space around the logo equal to half its height. A 32px logo needs 16px of space on
  every side.
- Do not stretch, crop, recolor or add effects to it.
- Do not use Squarespace's image editor on the logo. It saves images as .jpg, which turns the
  transparent background white. Upload the .png file as it is.

### The site icon (favicon)

The site icon, or favicon, is the small picture in the browser tab. Use the monogram.

1. Open **Settings**, then **Website**, then **Favicon**. (The help center links straight to this
   panel; on some accounts it is called **Browser icon**.)
2. Drag `masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png` into the uploader, or click it and choose the file.
3. Optional: add a dark mode version with `masschallenge-logo-monogram-white.png`. You must add the
   normal icon first.
4. Click **Save**.

Squarespace's limits: the file must be .png (recommended), under 100 KB, and works best between
100 and 300 pixels. The monogram file is 321 by 177 pixels and about 6 KB, so it uploads fine.
Because it is wider than it is tall, it shows small in the tab. If it looks squashed, place it in
the middle of a transparent square image (321 by 321 pixels) in any image editor and upload that.

Browsers hold on to old icons. If you still see the old one, clear your browser's cache or open the
site in a private window.

## Part 3: Build on brand pages

### Give each section its color

Every page is made of sections. Give each one a theme:

1. Open the **Pages** panel, click the page, and click **Edit**.
2. Hover over a section and click **Edit Section**.
3. Click **Colors** and choose:
   - **Lightest 1** for a White section,
   - **Light 1** for a Mist section,
   - **Darkest 1** for a Deep teal section.
4. Click **Save**.

Alternate White and Mist to separate sections, and use Deep teal sparingly for the moments that
matter, such as a call to apply.

A theme changes every color in the section, including any color you picked with the text toolbar.
Remember too that editing a theme changes every section on the site that uses it. That is what you
want: change Darkest 1 once and every Deep teal section follows.

### Section spacing

1. In **Edit Section**, click **Design** (it may be called **Format**).
2. Leave **Fill Screen** off unless you want a full height section.
3. In a Fluid Engine section, leave about one empty grid row above and below your content, and
   adjust **Row Count** until the space looks like about 96px on desktop. In a classic section, use
   **Section Height** and pick a small or medium height.
4. Keep text blocks to about 720px wide (roughly 68 characters a line). On a normal width page,
   that is a little over half the width of the grid. Long full width paragraphs are hard to read.
5. Check the mobile view: aim for about 64px of space above and below.

Squarespace does not let you type an exact pixel value for section spacing, so judge it by eye.

### Add the headline and text

1. Add a **Text** block.
2. Type your headline, select it, and choose **Heading 1** from the format menu in the text
   toolbar. Type it in normal sentence case: the capitals come from the Oswald style in Part 4, not
   from your keyboard.
3. Use **Heading 1** once per page, for the big headline only. Use **Heading 2** for section
   titles, **Heading 3** and **Heading 4** below that.
4. Use **Paragraph 2** for normal text, **Paragraph 1** for a short introduction under the
   headline, and **Paragraph 3** for small print such as dates.
5. Do not change fonts, sizes or colors with the toolbar. Let Site styles do it.

### Add buttons

1. Add a **Button** block.
2. In the **Content** tab, type the label. Use sentence case and a verb, such as "Apply now" or
   "Meet the startups".
3. In the **Design** tab, open the **Primary Button** dropdown:
   - Keep **Primary Button** for the main action (Teal).
   - Choose **Secondary Button** for a second, quieter action (Pale teal).
4. Under **Size**, choose **M**, the size that matches the padding you set in Part 1.
5. In a Fluid Engine section, set the button to **Fit** rather than **Fill**, so it keeps its pill
   shape and padding.

On a Deep teal section, buttons turn White with Deep teal text on their own, because of the
Darkest 1 theme. Use one primary button there.

### Sample home page

A simple page you can build in about fifteen minutes. Replace the bracketed text with your own.

1. **Hero, White (Lightest 1).** A Text block with your headline as Heading 1, then one or two
   sentences as Paragraph 1. Below it, a primary Button block ("[Main action]") and a secondary
   Button block ("[Second action]") side by side.
2. **What we do, Mist (Light 1).** A Heading 2 title. Under it, three short columns, each a Heading
   4 and a Paragraph 2. Add an image block above each column if you have photos.
3. **Proof, White (Lightest 1).** A Heading 2 and a short Paragraph 2, then a line of logos or a
   quote.
4. **Call to action, Deep teal (Darkest 1).** A Heading 2 and one sentence in Paragraph 1, with one
   primary Button block. It shows as a White button with Deep teal text.
5. **Footer.** Edit the footer section and give it **Lightest 1** or **Light 1**. If you add a logo
   to a Deep teal footer, use the white logo file.

## Part 4: Custom CSS (only what settings cannot do)

This part is optional. Your site is already on brand after Parts 1 to 3. Custom CSS is a few lines
of style code that you paste into one box; it adds three things that Squarespace settings cannot
do:

| Snippet | What it fixes | Why settings cannot do it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: the headline | Heading 1 in Oswald, medium weight, capitals, line height 1.0, letter spacing 1% | All heading sizes share one font and one capitals setting |
| B: button hovers | Primary hover turns Deep teal, secondary hover turns `#C4EEF4`, White buttons on Deep teal turn Pale teal | There is no hover color setting |
| C: exact headline sizes (optional) | Heading 1 at exactly 64px on desktop and 40px on phones | Squarespace scales headings with the screen, so sizes are close but not exact |

### Where to paste it

1. Open the **Pages** panel.
2. At the bottom, click **Custom Code**, then **Custom CSS**. (On some sites this is under
   **Design**, then **Custom CSS**, or **Website Tools**, then **Custom CSS**.)
3. Paste the snippets into the box. If the box already has code, paste snippet A at the very top,
   above everything else, and the others at the end.
4. Click **Save**.

The Custom CSS panel is available on every plan.

### Snippet A: the Oswald headline

```css
/* Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web */
@import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Oswald:wght@500&display=swap");

.sqs-block-html h1 {
  font-family: "Oswald", sans-serif;
  font-weight: 500;
  line-height: 1;
  letter-spacing: 0.01em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
}
```

What it does, line by line: the `@import` line loads Oswald from Google Fonts, the same place
Squarespace gets its fonts. The rest styles Heading 1, but only inside Text blocks (that is what
`.sqs-block-html` means). We target Text blocks on purpose: some built in pages, such as blog
posts and product pages, also use Heading 1 for their titles, and this keeps them in Lato.

The `@import` line must be the first rule in the box (the comment line above it is fine). If it is
lower down, browsers ignore it and the headline stays in Lato.

### Snippet B: button hover colors

```css
/* Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web */
.sqs-button-element--primary:hover {
  background-color: #044451 !important;
  opacity: 1 !important;
}

.sqs-button-element--secondary:hover {
  background-color: #c4eef4 !important;
  opacity: 1 !important;
}

[data-section-theme="black"] .sqs-button-element--primary:hover,
[data-section-theme="black"] .sqs-button-element--secondary:hover {
  background-color: #d9f6fa !important;
  color: #044451 !important;
}
```

`.sqs-button-element--primary` and `--secondary` are the names Squarespace gives primary and
secondary buttons. `!important` makes sure our hover wins over Squarespace's fade.
`[data-section-theme="black"]` is the name Squarespace uses behind the scenes for the **Darkest 1**
theme, so the last rule only touches buttons on Deep teal sections. If you chose a different theme
for Deep teal, this last rule will not apply; switch those sections to Darkest 1.

### Snippet C: exact headline sizes (optional)

```css
/* Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web */
.sqs-block-html h1 {
  font-size: 64px;
}

@media (max-width: 767px) {
  .sqs-block-html h1 {
    font-size: 40px;
  }
}
```

The second part applies only on screens 767px wide or narrower, which is where Squarespace switches
to its phone layout.

### Alternative: load the Propellant stylesheet (Core plan and above)

If your plan includes code injection, you can load the Propellant stylesheet instead of using
`@import`. It loads the exact Oswald and Lato files we use, and adds ready made classes.

1. Open the **Pages** panel, click **Custom Code**, then **Code Injection**.
2. In the **Header** box, paste:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/dist/website.css"
/>
```

3. Click **Save**.

The stylesheet only styles elements that carry one of its class names, so it never changes the
rest of your site. Squarespace's own blocks do not let you add class names, so you use the classes
inside a **Code** block, where you write a little HTML. For example:

```html
<h1 class="propellant-headline">Your headline here</h1>
<a class="propellant-button" href="/apply">Apply now</a>
<a class="propellant-button propellant-button-secondary" href="/about">Learn more</a>
```

`propellant-headline` is Heading 1 from the spec, `propellant-title-1`, `propellant-title-2` and
`propellant-title-3` are Headings 2 to 4, `propellant-body` is Paragraph and `propellant-caption`
is Paragraph small. A `<div class="propellant-brand-band">` wrapped around your HTML gives a Deep
teal band with White text and White buttons. The full list is in the
[website spec](/web/websites/#the-propellant-stylesheet). For most sites, snippets A and B are
simpler: they work with normal Text and Button blocks, so anyone can edit the page later.

### Removing the code later

Open **Custom Code**, then **Custom CSS** (or **Code Injection**), select the lines from the
`/* Propellant website styles` comment down to the end of that snippet, delete them and click
**Save**. Your site goes back to the plain Site styles from Part 1. Keep the comment line on
anything you leave in place, so the next person knows where it came from.

## Check your work

On a computer:

- [ ] Normal text and Headings 2 to 4 are in Lato. Heading 2 to 4 are bold.
- [ ] Heading 1 is in tall Oswald capitals (if you added snippet A), and it is the only text in
      capitals.
- [ ] Buttons are pills in sentence case: primary Teal with White text, secondary Pale teal with
      Teal text.
- [ ] Hovering a primary button turns it Deep teal (if you added snippet B).
- [ ] White, Mist and Deep teal sections each use Lightest 1, Light 1 and Darkest 1.
- [ ] Nothing on a Deep teal section is Teal. Text and buttons there are White.
- [ ] The full color logo sits on a White header, at least 24px tall, with room around it.
- [ ] The monogram shows in the browser tab.

On a phone (use the mobile view in the editor, then check the published site on a real phone):

- [ ] Heading 1 is about 40px and fits without breaking words awkwardly.
- [ ] The mobile logo is at least 24px tall.
- [ ] Buttons stay pill shaped and easy to tap.
- [ ] Sections have clear space above and below, about 64px.

Code can behave differently in the editor than on the live site. Open your published site in a
private window to see it the way visitors do.

## If something looks off

- **Heading 1 is still in Lato.** Check the text is set to Heading 1 in the format menu, not just
  made bigger. Check the `@import` line is the first rule in the Custom CSS box and that you clicked
  Save. Then reload the page.
- **One block ignores the site colors or fonts.** Someone styled it with the text toolbar. Select
  the text and clear the formatting, or pick the format again from the format menu, so it follows
  Site styles.
- **A whole section changed color after you edited the palette.** Palette changes flow into the
  color themes. Open Lightest 1, Light 1 and Darkest 1 again and re-enter the values from the table
  in Step 2.
- **Your fonts or buttons suddenly changed.** A theme or pack was clicked in Site styles. Use the
  undo arrow at the top of the panel, or set Step 1 or Step 3 again.
- **A button is square or stretched.** In a Fluid Engine section, set the Button block to **Fit**,
  not **Fill**. If all buttons are square, check **Shape** is **Pill** in Site styles, **Buttons**,
  for each button type.
- **The old browser icon still shows.** Browsers keep icons for a long time. Clear the cache or
  open the site in a private window.

# Webflow

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/webflow/

Webflow gives you everything you need to build a MassChallenge-style site without writing code.
You store the brand colors, fonts and sizes once as variables, style every heading, paragraph and
link at once, and make a handful of classes for buttons and sections. By the end you will have a
site with the right fonts, colors, headline, pill buttons, White, Mist and Deep teal sections, the
logo and a site icon, and it will look right on phones too. Plan on about two hours the first time,
most of it in Part 1.

Keep the [website spec](/web/websites/) open in another tab while you work. Every value in this
guide comes from it.

## Before you start

**Your plan.** You can do almost all of this guide on any Webflow plan, including the free one:

- Google Fonts, variables, tag styles and classes are part of the Designer (the Webflow editor).
  Webflow says you do not need a paid plan to use Google Fonts.
- Custom code (Part 4, optional) needs a paid Core, Growth, Agency or Freelancer Workspace, or an
  active Site plan on this site. You do not need custom code to follow the spec.
- Publishing to your own domain (such as yourdomain.org) needs a Site plan. Without one you can
  publish to a free `yoursite.webflow.io` address.

**Words you will meet.** Webflow uses a few terms from web design. Here is what they mean:

- **Variable**: a named, saved value, such as a color called Teal. Change it once and everything
  that uses it updates.
- **Tag style**: a style for every element of one kind, such as All H1 Headings. Webflow shows
  tags in pink.
- **Class**: a named style you give to chosen elements, such as a button. Webflow shows classes in
  blue.
- **Combo class**: a second class added after the first, which changes only a few things. A
  secondary button is the primary button class plus a combo class.
- **Breakpoint**: a screen width where your design can change, such as Mobile landscape.

**The logo files.** Download these from our public file store (right click each link, then save):

- Horizontal logo, full color, for White and Mist backgrounds:
  [masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png)
- Horizontal logo, white, for Deep teal backgrounds:
  [masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png)
- Monogram, full color, for the site icon:
  [masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png)

There are also `-black` versions of both lockups, and a `-white` monogram, at the same address. Use
these files only, never a copy of the logo from somewhere else. The
[brand guidelines](/brand/reference/) explain when to use each one.

## Part 1: Set up site styles (no code)

This is the heart of the guide. You will do it once, and every page you build afterwards starts
on brand.

### How Webflow styling works

Webflow styles in layers. The **Body (All Pages)** tag sets the defaults for the whole site. Tags
such as **All H1 Headings** and **All Paragraphs** then refine one kind of element. **Classes** sit
on top and change chosen elements, such as buttons and sections. Each layer only overrides what you
set on it, and everything else is inherited from the layer below.

**Variables** sit alongside this. You save each brand value once in the Variables panel and link
styles to it. You can then give a variable a second value for phones (a mode), so the mobile sizes
take care of themselves.

You do all of this in the **Style panel**, the panel on the right of the Designer. At the top of it
is the **Style selector** field, which shows what you are styling: a pink tag, a blue class or a
green state such as Hover.

### Step 1: Add Oswald

Lato is already built into the Webflow Designer, so you only need to add Oswald.

1. Open **Site settings**, then the **Fonts** tab.
2. Under **Google fonts**, choose **Oswald**.
3. Tick the **500** (Medium) variant. That is the only weight the headline uses.
4. Click **Add font**.
5. Go back to the Designer and refresh the page in your browser. Oswald now appears in **Style
   panel > Typography > Font**, under Google fonts.

You will not see Lato in the Site settings list. That is expected: Webflow leaves out the Google
fonts it already includes. Lato is in the Font dropdown under Google fonts.

> Webflow notes that its Google Fonts connection sends visitors' IP addresses to Google. If your
> privacy rules do not allow that, download Lato and Oswald from Google Fonts and upload them under
> **Site settings > Fonts > Custom fonts** instead. Everything else in this guide stays the same.

### Step 2: Make a Propellant variable collection

A collection keeps all the brand values together, so the next person can find them.

1. Open the **Variables** panel from the left toolbar of the Designer.
2. Click the **plus** icon next to **Site variables**.
3. Name the collection `Propellant` and click **Create**.

To add each variable below: click **New variable**, choose the type (Color, Size or Font Family),
then hover over the new variable's name and click the settings **cog** to rename it. Type the
name exactly as shown. The part before the slash puts it in a group, so `Colors/Teal` appears as
Teal inside a Colors group. Click the value to set it.

### Step 3: Add the color variables

Create one **Color** variable for each row. This is the full spec palette, plus the secondary
button hover color from the buttons table.

| Variable name | Hex | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Colors/White` | `#FFFFFF` | Page background, text on Deep teal |
| `Colors/Mist` | `#F3F6F7` | Alternate section background |
| `Colors/Ink` | `#1E282B` | Body text and headings |
| `Colors/Slate` | `#4B575B` | Secondary text, such as captions |
| `Colors/Teal` | `#065E6F` | Links and buttons |
| `Colors/Deep teal` | `#044451` | Button hover, and dark brand sections |
| `Colors/Bright teal` | `#0FACBD` | Accents on Deep teal sections only |
| `Colors/Pale teal` | `#D9F6FA` | Secondary buttons and tinted sections |
| `Colors/Pale teal hover` | `#C4EEF4` | Secondary button hover |
| `Colors/Line` | `#DBE1E3` | Lines and dividers |
| `Colors/Yellow` | `#FFC801` | Highlights, always with Ink text |
| `Colors/Magenta` | `#A30253` | Errors |

If your site already has swatches, Webflow has turned them into color variables. You can leave
them or delete the ones you no longer use.

### Step 4: Add the font variables

Create two **Font Family** variables:

| Variable name | Font |
| --- | --- |
| `Fonts/Body` | Lato |
| `Fonts/Headline` | Oswald |

### Step 5: Add the size variables

Create one **Size** variable for each row, using the **Desktop** value and the px unit. You will add
the Mobile values in the next step.

| Variable name | Desktop | Mobile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Type/Heading 1` | 64px | 40px |
| `Type/Heading 2` | 40px | 30px |
| `Type/Heading 3` | 30px | 24px |
| `Type/Heading 4` | 24px | 20px |
| `Type/Paragraph large` | 20px | 18px |
| `Type/Paragraph` | 17px | 16px |
| `Type/Paragraph small` | 14px | 14px |
| `Type/Button` | 16px | 16px |
| `Space/Section` | 96px | 64px |
| `Space/Button vertical` | 14px | 14px |
| `Space/Button horizontal` | 28px | 28px |
| `Layout/Text width` | 720px | 720px |
| `Radius/Card` | 12px | 12px |
| `Radius/Pill` | 9999px | 9999px |

`Radius/Pill` is a very large corner radius, which is how a web page draws fully rounded pill
ends. `Layout/Text width` keeps paragraphs to about 68 characters a line.

### Step 6: Add the mobile sizes with a mode

A mode is a second set of values for the same variables. A responsive mode switches on by itself at
a breakpoint, so you link each style once and it shrinks on phones automatically.

1. In the Variables panel, with the Propellant collection open, click the **New mode** dropdown
   arrow.
2. Name the mode `Mobile`.
3. In the **Responsive** dropdown, choose **Mobile landscape**. That covers screens 767px wide and
   below, which includes phones held either way.
4. Click **Create**. Every value starts as a copy of the Base (desktop) value.
5. In the Mobile column, click each value that changes and type the Mobile number from the table
   in Step 5: Heading 1 40px, Heading 2 30px, Heading 3 24px, Heading 4 20px, Paragraph large 18px,
   Paragraph 16px and Section 64px. Leave the others as they are.

You will check this on the Mobile portrait breakpoint in "Check your work".

### Step 7: Style the Body (All Pages) tag

These are the defaults every page inherits.

1. Open any page and click the **Body** element in the Navigator (the page structure list on the
   left).
2. In the Style panel, click the **Style selector** field. Under **HTML Tag**, choose **Body (All
   Pages)**.
3. Under **Typography**, set:
   - **Font**: hover over the field, click the purple dot in its top left corner and choose
     `Fonts/Body`. (This purple dot is how you link any field to a variable.)
   - **Weight**: 400 (Normal).
   - **Size**: link to `Type/Paragraph`.
   - **Height** (line height): type `1.6`, then choose the **-** unit so it has no unit. A unitless
     line height grows and shrinks with the text.
   - **Color**: link to `Colors/Ink`.
4. Under **Backgrounds**, set **Color** to `Colors/White`.

Set the text color here, on the Body, and not on the heading and paragraph tags. That way a Deep
teal section can switch all its text to White in one place (Part 3).

### Step 8: Style All H1 to All H4 headings

Add a Heading to any page from **Add panel > Typography** so you have one to click. Select it, make
sure it has no class, then open the Style selector field and choose the tag. Set each tag as
below, and link the font and size to the variables shown.

| Tag | Font | Weight | Size | Height | Letter spacing | Letter case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| All H1 Headings | `Fonts/Headline` | 500 (Medium) | `Type/Heading 1` | `1` (no unit) | `0.01em` | All capitals |
| All H2 Headings | `Fonts/Body` | 700 (Bold) | `Type/Heading 2` | `1.15` (no unit) | leave empty | leave empty |
| All H3 Headings | `Fonts/Body` | 700 (Bold) | `Type/Heading 3` | `1.2` (no unit) | leave empty | leave empty |
| All H4 Headings | `Fonts/Body` | 700 (Bold) | `Type/Heading 4` | `1.25` (no unit) | leave empty | leave empty |

To change which heading level you are styling, select the heading and change its level (H1, H2
and so on) in the Settings panel, or add one heading of each level and select each in turn.

For the H1 headline:

- **Letter spacing** and **letter case** are under **More type options** at the bottom of the
  Typography section. Type `0.01em` (that is the spec's 1%) for letter spacing, and choose the
  all capitals option (shown as **AA**) for letter case.
- Type your headline in sentence case, such as "Founders build here". Webflow turns it into
  capitals for you. Screen readers then read words, not letters.
- If you cannot find the letter case control, use **Style panel > Custom properties** instead:
  click **Add**, type `text-transform` as the name and `uppercase` as the value, and press Enter.

Leave the color empty on all four tags, so they inherit Ink from the Body.

### Step 9: Style All Paragraphs and All Links

**All Paragraphs.** Select a paragraph with no class, open the Style selector field and choose
**All Paragraphs**. Set:

- **Size**: link to `Type/Paragraph`.
- **Height**: `1.6` (no unit).
- **Size section > Max W** (maximum width): link to `Layout/Text width`.

**All Links.** Select a text link, open the Style selector field and choose **All Links**. Set:

- **Color**: link to `Colors/Teal`.
- **Decoration**: underline.

Webflow treats buttons as links too, so buttons start out teal and underlined. The button classes
in Step 11 fix that.

### Step 10: Make the paragraph size classes

The spec has two more text sizes, so make a class for each. Select a paragraph, click the Style
selector field, type the class name and press Enter. Then set:

| Class | Size | Height | Color |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paragraph-large` | `Type/Paragraph large` | `1.5` (no unit) | leave empty |
| `paragraph-small` | `Type/Paragraph small` | `1.5` (no unit) | `Colors/Slate` (for captions) |

### Step 11: Make the button classes

You will make one base class for the primary button, then two combo classes for the other button
styles. Webflow buttons come from **Add panel > Links > Button**.

**Primary button: `brand-button`.** Add a Button, click the Style selector field, type
`brand-button` and press Enter. Set:

- **Typography**: Font `Fonts/Body`, Weight 700 (Bold), Size `Type/Button`, Height `1` (no unit),
  Color `Colors/White`, Decoration none (click the **X**).
- **Backgrounds**: Color `Colors/Teal`.
- **Spacing**: padding top and bottom `Space/Button vertical`, left and right
  `Space/Button horizontal`.
- **Borders**: Radius `Radius/Pill`. No border width and no shadow.

Now the hover color. Click the dropdown arrow in the Style selector field, choose **Hover** from
the **States** menu (a green Hover label appears), and set **Backgrounds > Color** to
`Colors/Deep teal`. Choose **None** in the same menu to go back to the normal state.

**Secondary button: `brand-button` plus `is-secondary`.** Add a second Button. Type
`brand-button`, press Enter, then type `is-secondary` and press Enter. The second class is a combo
class: it starts with everything from `brand-button` and only changes what you set here.

- **Backgrounds**: Color `Colors/Pale teal`.
- **Typography**: Color `Colors/Teal`.
- **Hover** state: Backgrounds Color `Colors/Pale teal hover`.

**Button on Deep teal: `brand-button` plus `is-on-dark`.** Add a third Button, apply
`brand-button`, then the combo class `is-on-dark`:

- **Backgrounds**: Color `Colors/White`.
- **Typography**: Color `Colors/Deep teal`.
- **Hover** state: Backgrounds Color `Colors/Pale teal`.

Write button labels in sentence case with a verb, such as "Apply now" or "Meet the startups".

### Step 12: Make the section classes

Sections work the same way: one base class and two combo classes.

1. From **Add panel > Structure**, add a **Box**. (In older versions of Webflow, add a **Section**
   instead and skip the next step.)
2. In the **Settings** panel, set the **Tag** to **Section**.
3. Click the Style selector field, type `brand-section` and press Enter. Set:
   - **Spacing**: padding top and bottom `Space/Section`.
   - **Backgrounds**: Color `Colors/White`.
4. Add a second section with `brand-section` plus the combo class `is-mist`, and set
   **Backgrounds > Color** to `Colors/Mist`.
5. Add a third section with `brand-section` plus the combo class `is-deep-teal`, and set
   **Backgrounds > Color** to `Colors/Deep teal` and **Typography > Color** to `Colors/White`.
   Headings and paragraphs inside it turn White, because they inherit their color.

**Links on Deep teal.** Text links keep their Teal color, and Teal on Deep teal is not allowed.
Give any text link inside a Deep teal section the class `link-on-dark` and set its
**Typography > Color** to `Colors/White`. For a small accent on Deep teal, such as an icon or a
short label, use `Colors/Bright teal`.

### Step 13: Round images and cards

Select an image, open the Style selector field and choose **All Images**. Set **Borders > Radius**
to `Radius/Card`. Do the same on any card class you make later.

### Step 14 (only if needed): Mobile without modes

The Mobile mode in Step 6 should handle phone sizes everywhere. If a size does not change on a
phone, set it directly: click the **Mobile landscape** icon in the canvas bar (above the canvas),
select the element, choose the same tag or class in the Style selector, and type the Mobile value
from the table in Step 5. Styles set on Mobile landscape also apply to Mobile portrait.

## Part 2: Add the logo and site icon

### The logo

In Webflow the logo is part of the page, in the navigation bar, rather than a site setting.

1. Open the **Assets** panel in the left toolbar, click the **cloud** icon and upload the
   horizontal color logo (and the white one, if you will use a Deep teal footer).
2. From **Add panel > Other**, drag a **Navbar** to the top of your page.
3. Drag the color logo from the Assets panel into the Navbar's **Brand** link.
4. Select the logo image and set **Style panel > Size > Height** to `32px`, with width left on
   Auto so the proportions stay right. Never go below 24px tall; on very small spaces use the
   monogram instead.
5. In the image's settings, set the alt text (the description screen readers announce) to
   `MassChallenge`.
6. Select the Brand link, open **Settings panel > Link settings**, choose **Page** and pick your
   home page.

Keep clear space around the logo of at least half its height (16px for a 32px logo). Do not
stretch, recolor or add effects. On a Deep teal background, use the white logo.

To make the Navbar appear on every page, right click it and turn it into a component, then add that
component to each page.

### The site icon (favicon)

The site icon is the little picture in the browser tab. Webflow needs one square image and makes
every size from it.

1. Make the monogram square first. The monogram file is wider than it is tall, so open it in any
   image editor, put it in the middle of a square transparent canvas, and add empty space above
   and below. Do not stretch or crop it.
2. Open **Site settings > General > Icons** and click **Upload icon**.
3. Upload your square monogram and select which icons to update.
4. Click **Apply**, then publish your site and refresh it in your browser to see the new icon.

## Part 3: Build on brand pages

With Part 1 done, building a page is mostly a matter of choosing the right class. The quickest way
to apply a class is to select an element, click the Style selector field (or press Command + Enter
on a Mac, Control + Enter on Windows), start typing the name and press Enter.

| You want | Element | Classes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A White section | Box with the Section tag | `brand-section` |
| A Mist section | Box with the Section tag | `brand-section` `is-mist` |
| A Deep teal section | Box with the Section tag | `brand-section` `is-deep-teal` |
| The big headline | Heading set to H1 | none (the tag does it) |
| A primary button | Button | `brand-button` |
| A secondary button | Button | `brand-button` `is-secondary` |
| A button on Deep teal | Button | `brand-button` `is-on-dark` |
| A link on Deep teal | Text link | `link-on-dark` |
| An intro paragraph | Paragraph | `paragraph-large` |
| A caption or note | Paragraph | `paragraph-small` |

To apply a combo class, apply the base class first, then type the combo class name. Typing a
comma after the first name adds it and lets you type the next one straight away.

A few rules from the spec to keep in mind:

- Use one H1 per page, for the big headline. Use H2, H3 and H4 for everything below it.
- Never put Teal text or a primary button on Deep teal. Use White text and the `is-on-dark` button.
- Yellow is for highlights only, and always with Ink text on it.

### Build a sample home page

1. Add the Navbar component with the logo at the top.
2. **Hero, on White.** Add a `brand-section`. Inside it, add a Heading set to H1 (for example
   "Founders build here"), a paragraph with `paragraph-large`, and two Buttons: one `brand-button`
   ("Apply now") and one `brand-button` `is-secondary` ("Learn more").
3. **Story, on Mist.** Add a `brand-section` `is-mist` with an H2, two paragraphs and an image.
4. **Call to action, on Deep teal.** Add a `brand-section` `is-deep-teal` with an H2, a paragraph and
   a `brand-button` `is-on-dark` button.
5. **Footer.** Add a `brand-section` `is-deep-teal` with the white logo and your links, each with
   `link-on-dark`.
6. Click **Preview** (the eye icon) to see the page as a visitor would, then switch to the Mobile
   landscape and Mobile portrait breakpoints in the canvas bar to check phones.

To keep content from running edge to edge on wide screens, put a Box inside each section and give
it a maximum width and Auto left and right margins. The spec does not set a page width, so choose
one that suits your layout and use it for every section.

### Publish

1. Click **Publish** at the top right of the Designer (or press Shift + P).
2. Tick the domain(s) to publish to: your `webflow.io` address, your own domain, or both.
3. Click **Publish to selected domains**.

To try changes before they go public, tick only the `webflow.io` address.

## Part 4: Custom code (optional)

**You do not need custom code for Webflow.** Parts 1 to 3 cover the whole spec with Webflow's own
variables, tags and classes, and those are the better choice: the next person can see and change
them in the Style panel, and they show on the canvas while you edit. If you ever need a style that
the Style panel has no control for, add it under **Style panel > Custom properties** on the class
or tag. That is still no code to maintain.

### Alternative: the Propellant stylesheet

If you would rather use our ready made classes than build your own, you can load the Propellant
stylesheet and type its class names into Webflow. Use this instead of Steps 10 to 12 of Part 1, not
as well as them. You still need Step 1 (Oswald), and the tag styles from Steps 7 to 9 are still
worth doing.

This needs a paid Core, Growth, Agency or Freelancer Workspace, or an active Site plan.

1. Open **Site settings**, then the **Custom code** tab.
2. Paste this into the **Head code** box:

   ```html
   <!-- Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web -->
   <link
     rel="stylesheet"
     href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/dist/website.css"
   />
   ```

   The first line is a label, so the next person knows where the code came from. Keep it.

3. Click **Save changes**, then publish.
4. In the Designer, select an element, click the Style selector field, type one of the class names
   below and press Enter. Do not add any styles to these classes in the Style panel; the
   stylesheet does that.

| On this element | Type this class | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heading set to H1 | `propellant-headline` | The Oswald capitals headline |
| Button | `propellant-button` | The primary pill button |
| Button | `propellant-button`, then `propellant-button-secondary` | The secondary button |
| Box with the Section tag | `propellant-brand-band` | A Deep teal section with White text and White buttons |
| Text link | `propellant-link` | A teal, underlined link |
| Paragraph | `propellant-body` | Paragraph text |
| Paragraph | `propellant-caption` | Small print, such as dates and notes |
| Section or Box | `propellant-text` | The body font and text color for a whole section |

Things to know:

- The stylesheet's styles appear in **Preview** and on the published site, but you may not see
  them on the canvas while you edit. That is why Webflow's own classes are easier to work with.
- The stylesheet uses the same values as the spec and loads Lato and Oswald itself. Keep Oswald
  in Site settings > Fonts anyway, so it also shows on the canvas while you edit.

**To remove it later:** take the `propellant-` classes off your elements (click the class in the
Style selector and press Delete), delete the lines from **Site settings > Custom code > Head
code**, click **Save changes** and publish again.

## Check your work

On desktop, in Preview and on the published site:

- [ ] The H1 headline is Oswald, in capitals, 64px, and there is only one per page.
- [ ] H2 to H4 and all body text are Lato, in sentence case, in Ink.
- [ ] Links are Teal and underlined, and none sit on Deep teal.
- [ ] Primary buttons are Teal pills with White text and turn Deep teal on hover.
- [ ] Secondary buttons are Pale teal pills with Teal text.
- [ ] Deep teal sections have White text, White buttons and the white logo.
- [ ] Sections have about 96px of space above and below, and paragraphs stop at about 720px wide.
- [ ] The logo is the official file, at least 24px tall, and links to the home page.
- [ ] The site icon shows the monogram in the browser tab.

On a phone (or the Mobile landscape and Mobile portrait breakpoints):

- [ ] The H1 is 40px, H2 30px, H3 24px, H4 20px and paragraphs 16px.
- [ ] Sections have about 64px of space above and below.
- [ ] Buttons stay pills and their labels fit on one line.

## If something looks off

- **Headings are still in Webflow's default font or size.** The heading probably has a class with
  its own font or size. Select it, look at the Style selector, and remove the class (or reset the
  font and size on it) so it falls back to the All H1 to All H4 tags.
- **Text in a Deep teal section is dark.** The color was set on a heading or paragraph tag or class
  rather than on the Body. Clear the color there (click the blue or pink label next to Color and
  choose Reset) so it inherits White from the section.
- **Buttons are underlined or turn a different color on hover.** Buttons inherit from All Links.
  Select the button, set **Decoration** to none on `brand-button`, and check that the Hover state
  is set on the button class, not only on All Links.
- **Sizes do not shrink on phones.** Check that the Mobile mode in the Variables panel has its
  Responsive setting on Mobile landscape, and that the style is linked to a variable (the value
  shows in purple). If it shows a plain number, link it to the variable, or use Step 14.
- **Oswald is missing from the Font list.** Refresh the Designer after adding it in Site settings.
  If it is still missing, check that it is listed under **Site settings > Fonts > Google fonts**.
- **The stylesheet classes do nothing.** Custom code only runs in Preview and on the published
  site, and only after you save it and publish. Check that the code is in Head code, not Footer
  code, and that your plan includes custom code.

# Wix

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/wix/

This guide gives a Wix site the MassChallenge look: Lato and Oswald type, the teal palette, pill
shaped buttons and the right logo in the header. It covers both of Wix's editors, the Wix Editor
and Wix Studio, and says clearly where they differ. Setting up the styles takes about an hour. Plan
on another hour if you are building a home page from scratch.

Wix has more than one editor, and each puts the style settings in a different place. Check which
one you have before you start:

- **Wix Editor** (the classic editor): the left side of the screen has a **Site Design** button
  (called Theme Manager in some older versions).
- **Wix Studio**: the left side of the screen has a **Site Styles** button.
- If you see a **Brand** button at the top of the editor instead, your site uses Wix's newer
  editor (Wix Harmony). The values in this guide still apply: enter them under **Brand**, then
  **Colors**, **Text** and **Buttons**.

## Before you start

**Plans.** You can do almost everything in this guide on any Wix plan, free included. A few steps
need more:

| Step | Wix Editor | Wix Studio |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Site styles, logo, sections and buttons (Parts 1 to 3) | Any plan | Any plan |
| Site icon (favicon, the small picture in the browser tab) | Paid (Premium) plan, a connected domain and a published site | Same as Wix Editor |
| CSS editing in `global.css` (Part 4) | Usually not available (see Part 4) | Available in the editor's Code panel. Wix's help pages list no plan requirement |
| Custom code in the page head (Part 5) | Published site with a connected domain, which needs a paid plan | Same as Wix Editor |

A connected domain means your own web address, such as `yourname.org`, instead of a free
`wixsite.com` address. Wix only lets you connect one on a paid plan.

**Keep the spec open.** Every value in this guide comes from the
[website spec](/web/websites/). Open it in a second browser tab so you can copy hex codes (the six
character color codes that start with `#`) straight from it.

**Download the logo files.** Use only the official files. Save these to your computer:

- [masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png),
  for white and light backgrounds.
- [masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png),
  for Deep teal sections and dark photos.
- [masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v1.1.1/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png),
  for the site icon.

There are also `-black` versions of both lockups (for example
`masschallenge-logo-horizontal-black.png`) at the same address, for places where only one dark
color works. Read the [logo rules](/brand/reference/#logo) once before you place the logo: never
stretch, recolor or crop it.

## Part 1: Set up site styles (no code)

This is where most of the work happens. Set the styles once and every themed element on the site
picks them up. Follow the section for your editor.

### Wix Editor

The Wix Editor has three site-wide settings: a **color theme**, a **text theme** (named text
styles: Heading 1 to Heading 6 and Paragraph 1 to Paragraph 3) and the colors for **primary and
secondary buttons**. Button shape and padding are set on a button itself, then copied.

#### Step 1: Set the theme colors

The color theme has two kinds of color. **Base colors** run from light to dark: Wix uses the
lightest for backgrounds and the darkest for text, and builds a range of shades between them.
**Accent colors** are used for links, buttons and menus.

1. In the editor, click **Site Design** on the left.
2. Click **Color theme**. In some versions you hover over **Color & Text Theme** and click
   **Customize** instead.
3. Click a color in the panel, type its hex code into the HEX field, and click **Apply**. Set them
   from this table:

   | Wix slot | Spec color | Hex |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Base color, lightest (backgrounds) | White | `#FFFFFF` |
   | Base color, darkest (text) | Ink | `#1E282B` |
   | Accent color 1 | Teal | `#065E6F` |
   | Accent color 2 | Deep teal | `#044451` |
   | Accent color 3 | Pale teal | `#D9F6FA` |
   | Accent color 4 | Bright teal | `#0FACBD` |

   If your panel shows fewer accent slots, fill them in this order and stop when you run out.
   If it shows more, use Mist `#F3F6F7` and Slate `#4B575B` next.

4. Open **Advanced Settings** (at the bottom of the color panel). Click the color box next to each
   item and set:

   | Group | Item | Spec color | Hex |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | General | Primary background | White | `#FFFFFF` |
   | General | Secondary background | Mist | `#F3F6F7` |
   | General | Lines and dividers | Line | `#DBE1E3` |
   | Text | Titles and paragraphs | Ink | `#1E282B` |
   | Text | Subtitles | Slate | `#4B575B` |
   | Text | Links | Teal | `#065E6F` |
   | Buttons | Primary, regular | Teal | `#065E6F` |
   | Buttons | Primary, hover | Deep teal | `#044451` |
   | Buttons | Secondary, regular | Pale teal | `#D9F6FA` |
   | Buttons | Secondary, hover | (secondary hover) | `#C4EEF4` |
   | Buttons | Disabled | Line | `#DBE1E3` |

   The exact item names in this panel vary between sites. Match each item to the closest row.
   If the panel also asks for button text colors, use White `#FFFFFF` on primary buttons and Teal
   `#065E6F` on secondary buttons.

5. Save the remaining spec colors so they are one click away later: Mist `#F3F6F7`, Slate
   `#4B575B`, Line `#DBE1E3`, Yellow `#FFC801` and Magenta `#A30253`. In any color picker, use
   **My colors** and the add option (a plus sign) to save each one.

Only use Bright teal on Deep teal sections, and only use Yellow behind Ink text. Magenta is for
error messages, never decoration.

#### Step 2: Check that Lato and Oswald are in your font list

1. Select any text box on the page and click **Edit Text**.
2. Open the **Fonts** drop-down and look for **Lato** and **Oswald**. Wix lists font weights as
   separate entries in some cases, so you may see **Oswald Medium** listed on its own. That is the
   one you want for Heading 1.
3. If either font is missing, upload it:
   1. Download the font from Google Fonts ([Lato](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Lato) and
      [Oswald](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Oswald)). You need Lato Regular, Lato Bold and
      Oswald Medium.
   2. In the same **Fonts** drop-down, click **Upload Fonts** and choose the file (TTF, OTF, WOFF
      or WOFF2 all work).
   3. Click **Done** when it finishes. Uploaded fonts appear under **My Fonts** in the drop-down.

Uploaded fonts do not work in the Wix Blog and some Wix apps, so prefer the built-in Lato and
Oswald when they are listed.

#### Step 3: Set the text theme

1. Click **Site Design**, then **Text theme**.
2. Set **Heading Font** to **Lato** and **Paragraph Font** to **Lato**. Heading 1 gets Oswald in
   the next step.
3. Click **Customize heading styles**. Hover over each style, click the edit (pencil) icon, and
   enter the values from the table below. Then do the same under **Customize paragraph styles**.

| Wix style | Spec style | Font | Bold | Size | Line spacing | Character spacing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | Heading 1 | Oswald Medium (or Oswald, not bold) | Off | 64px | 1.0 | 0.01em (1%) |
| Heading 2 | Heading 2 | Lato | On | 40px | 1.15 | 0 |
| Heading 3 | Heading 3 | Lato | On | 30px | 1.2 | 0 |
| Heading 4 | Heading 4 | Lato | On | 24px | 1.25 | 0 |
| Heading 5 | Heading 4 | Lato | On | 24px | 1.25 | 0 |
| Heading 6 | Heading 4 | Lato | On | 24px | 1.25 | 0 |
| Paragraph 1 | Paragraph large | Lato | Off | 20px | 1.5 | 0 |
| Paragraph 2 | Paragraph | Lato | Off | 17px | 1.6 | 0 |
| Paragraph 3 | Paragraph small | Lato | Off | 14px | 1.5 | 0 |

Notes on the fields:

- **Line spacing.** Wix may show this as a number (enter the value above) or in pixels. For pixels,
  multiply the size by the line spacing: 64px for Heading 1, 46px for Heading 2, 36px for Heading
  3, 30px for Heading 4 and Paragraph 1, 27px for Paragraph 2 and 21px for Paragraph 3.
- **Character spacing.** Only Heading 1 has any. If the field takes a small decimal, enter
  `0.01`. If it takes a percentage, enter `1`.
- **Color.** Leave every style on Ink `#1E282B` (the darkest base color). Do not make headings teal:
  teal means something you can click.
- **Heading 5 and 6** have no style of their own in the spec, so they copy Heading 4. Keep them out
  of your pages if you can.
- **Capitals.** The Wix Editor has no setting that turns a style into capitals. Type your Heading 1
  text in capitals, for example BUILT FOR THE WORLD. Type every other heading and button in
  sentence case (capital first letter, the rest lower case except names).

Any change to a style updates all the text on the site that already uses it.

#### Step 4: Design one primary button and one secondary button

The Wix Editor has no site-wide button shape setting, so you style one button and reuse it.

1. Click **Add Elements** on the left, then **Button**, and add a **Themed** button so it picks up
   your theme colors.
2. Select the button, click the **Design** icon, then **Customize Design**.
3. Set the **Regular** state:
   - **Fill:** Teal `#065E6F`, opacity 100%.
   - **Borders:** width 0.
   - **Corners:** click the lock so all four corners change together, then enter `100`. Any number
     at least half the button's height makes the fully rounded pill ends.
   - **Shadows:** off.
   - **Text:** Lato, 16px, bold, White `#FFFFFF`, character spacing 0.
   - **Layout:** padding of about 14px above and below the text and 28px on each side. If your
     button only offers side padding, set 28px there and make the button about 44px tall.
4. Switch to the **Hover** state and set **Fill** to Deep teal `#044451`. Keep the text White.
5. Type a label in sentence case with a verb, such as Apply now.
6. For a **secondary** button, duplicate the primary button (copy and paste it) and change only the
   colors: Regular fill Pale teal `#D9F6FA`, text Teal `#065E6F`. Hover fill `#C4EEF4`, text Teal.
7. Keep these two buttons on a spare page or in a hidden spot. Copy and paste them whenever you
   need a new button, so every button stays the same.

#### Step 5: Set the mobile sizes

The Wix Editor has a separate mobile editor. Changes you make there only affect phones. Text you
added on desktop keeps its wording, but you can change its size on mobile.

1. Click the phone icon at the top of the editor to switch to the mobile view.
2. Select each heading and paragraph and set its size to the mobile value:

| Style | Mobile size |
| --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | 40px |
| Heading 2 | 30px |
| Heading 3 | 24px |
| Heading 4 | 20px |
| Paragraph large (Paragraph 1) | 18px |
| Paragraph (Paragraph 2) | 16px |
| Paragraph small (Paragraph 3) | 14px |
| Button text | 16px |

3. Check that buttons stay pill shaped and that sections have about 64px of space above and below
   their content.

### Wix Studio

Wix Studio keeps colors and text styles in one panel called **Site Styles**. It has no site-wide
button style yet, so buttons are styled one at a time or, better, with the short CSS in Part 4.

#### Step 1: Set the site colors

Every Studio site has at least six numbered colors, each tied to a job across the site and its
apps. You can add more, up to 25.

1. Click **Site Styles** on the left side of the editor, then the **Colors** tab.
2. Click a color, type the hex code into the HEX field, and click **Apply**. Set them from this
   table:

   | Studio color | What Wix uses it for | Spec color | Hex |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | Color 1 | Primary background | White | `#FFFFFF` |
   | Color 2 | Secondary background | Mist | `#F3F6F7` |
   | Color 3 | Disabled items | Line | `#DBE1E3` |
   | Color 4 | Secondary text | Slate | `#4B575B` |
   | Color 5 | Primary text | Ink | `#1E282B` |
   | Color 6 | Links and actions | Teal | `#065E6F` |

   Your template may give these colors names, such as Primary background. Go by the job, not the
   name.

3. Add the rest of the spec palette as extra site colors, and rename each one to its spec name
   (hover over a color, click the **More Actions** icon, then **Rename**):

   | Name | Hex |
   | --- | --- |
   | Deep teal | `#044451` |
   | Bright teal | `#0FACBD` |
   | Pale teal | `#D9F6FA` |
   | Secondary hover | `#C4EEF4` |
   | Yellow | `#FFC801` |
   | Magenta | `#A30253` |

#### Step 2: Set the fonts

1. In **Site Styles**, open the **Typography** tab.
2. Under **Fonts**, click each font, choose **Lato** from the drop-down, and click **Update**.
   Heading 1 gets Oswald in the next step.
3. If Lato or Oswald is missing from the list, upload it:
   1. Download it from Google Fonts ([Lato](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Lato) and
      [Oswald](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Oswald)).
   2. Select any text element, click the **Open Inspector** icon at the top right, scroll to
      **Design** and open the **Font** drop-down.
   3. Click **Upload fonts** at the bottom, then **Upload Fonts**, and choose the file (TTF, OTF,
      WOFF or WOFF2). Click **Close** when it is done. It now appears under **Uploaded fonts**.

#### Step 3: Set the text styles

Studio has nine text styles: Heading 1 to Heading 6 (H1 to H6) and Paragraph 1 to Paragraph 3.
Each one has a **scale** option that sets a largest and smallest size, so the text shrinks
smoothly on small screens. That is how you set the mobile sizes.

1. In **Site Styles**, **Typography**, under **Text styles**, click a style.
2. Set the font, weight, size, line spacing, character spacing and color from the table below.
3. Turn on **scale** and enter the largest size as the maximum and the mobile size as the minimum.
4. Click the arrow at the top left to go back, and do the next style.

| Studio style | Spec style | Font and weight | Max size | Min size | Line spacing | Character spacing | Color |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | Heading 1 | Oswald, Medium (500) | 64px | 40px | 1.0 | 0.01em (1%) | Ink |
| Heading 2 | Heading 2 | Lato, Bold (700) | 40px | 30px | 1.15 | 0 | Ink |
| Heading 3 | Heading 3 | Lato, Bold (700) | 30px | 24px | 1.2 | 0 | Ink |
| Heading 4 | Heading 4 | Lato, Bold (700) | 24px | 20px | 1.25 | 0 | Ink |
| Heading 5 | Heading 4 | Lato, Bold (700) | 24px | 20px | 1.25 | 0 | Ink |
| Heading 6 | Heading 4 | Lato, Bold (700) | 24px | 20px | 1.25 | 0 | Ink |
| Paragraph 1 | Paragraph large | Lato, Regular (400) | 20px | 18px | 1.5 | 0 | Ink |
| Paragraph 2 | Paragraph | Lato, Regular (400) | 17px | 16px | 1.6 | 0 | Ink |
| Paragraph 3 | Paragraph small | Lato, Regular (400) | 14px | 14px | 1.5 | 0 | Ink |

If the style panel only offers a **Bold** switch rather than a weight list, turn Bold on for the
Lato headings and off for paragraphs, and for Heading 1 pick **Oswald Medium** from the font list
if it is there (uploaded or built in). If line spacing is in pixels, use the pixel values from the
Wix Editor notes above. Studio, like the Wix Editor, has no capitals setting in Site Styles: type
the Heading 1 text in capitals, or add the short CSS in Part 4 so Wix does it for you.

#### Step 4: Style your buttons

Site Styles does not include buttons yet (Wix lists it as a feature request). You have two
options:

- **Recommended: use the button CSS in Part 4.** It styles every button on the site in one go and
  keeps them consistent.
- **Without code:** select a button, click **Open Inspector**, and under **Design** set the same
  values as the Wix Editor button in Step 4 above: Teal fill, White Lato 16px bold text, no
  border, no shadow, corners of `100`, padding of about 14px by 28px, and a Deep teal hover. Then
  copy and paste that button wherever you need one.

#### Step 5: Check the mobile breakpoint

Studio shows a desktop, tablet and mobile view at the top of the editor. These are breakpoints:
the screen widths where the layout can change.

1. Click the mobile view.
2. Check that the text has shrunk to the minimum sizes you set.
3. Select each section and set about 64px of space above and below its content (96px on
   desktop).

## Part 2: Add the logo and site icon

### The logo in the header

The steps are close to identical in both editors.

1. Click the header at the top of any page, so you edit the header shared by every page.
2. Add an image: in the Wix Editor, click **Add Elements**, then **Image**. In Wix Studio, use the
   add panel on the left. Upload `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png`.
3. Place it at the left of the header, lined up with the content below it.
4. Resize it by dragging a corner, never a side, so it keeps its shape. Keep it at least 24px tall.
   About 32px tall is a good header size.
5. Leave clear space around it equal to half its height (16px for a 32px logo). No text, edge or
   other image inside that space.
6. Link it to the home page: select the logo, click the link icon, choose **Page**, then **Home**.
7. Give it alt text (the description screen readers read out) of `MassChallenge`. In the Wix
   Editor this is in the image **Settings**. In Studio it is in the **Inspector**.

If your header is Deep teal or a dark photo, use `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png`
instead. Never place the full color logo on Deep teal.

### The site icon (favicon)

The site icon needs a paid plan, a connected domain and a published site. Wix needs a square image
whose sides are a multiple of 48px. The monogram file is wider than it is tall, so make a square
version first:

1. In any image editor, make a new square canvas of 192 by 192 pixels with a transparent
   background.
2. Place `masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png` in the middle, scaled down so it does not touch
   the edges. Do not stretch it.
3. Export it as a PNG.

Then upload it:

1. Go to your site's dashboard and click **Settings**.
2. Click **Website settings**.
3. Under **Favicon**, click **Upload Image**, choose your PNG, and save.

Search engines decide whether and when to show the new icon in results, so it may take a while to
appear there.

## Part 3: Build on brand pages

A MassChallenge page alternates between three kinds of section. Stack them so neighboring sections
differ, and keep the Deep teal section for the moments that matter most, such as the opening or the
final call to action.

### Make the three kinds of section

**White section** (the default):

- **Wix Editor:** right-click the section (or click a strip) and choose **Change Background**.
  Under **Color**, pick White `#FFFFFF`.
- **Wix Studio:** select the section, click **Open Inspector**, click the color box under
  **Design** and pick Color 1 (White).

**Mist section** (for alternating sections):

- The same steps, with Mist `#F3F6F7`. In Studio it is Color 2.

**Deep teal section** (the brand band):

1. Set the background to Deep teal `#044451` the same way.
2. Set every heading and paragraph in it to White `#FFFFFF`: select the text and change its color.
3. Use Bright teal `#0FACBD` for any small accent, such as a short line or an icon. Never put Teal
   `#065E6F` text on Deep teal.
4. Use the white logo if the logo appears here.
5. Style the buttons as described in "Buttons on Deep teal" below.

In Studio, a section's background can differ by breakpoint. Check the mobile view to make sure it
stayed the same.

### Section spacing and width

- Give each section about 96px of empty space above and below its content on desktop and 64px on
  mobile.
- Make paragraph text boxes about 720px wide, so lines run to roughly 68 characters. Drag the side
  of the text box, or set the width in Studio's Inspector.
- Round images and cards by 12px: select the image, open its design settings, and set **Corners**
  to 12.

### Add the Heading 1 headline

1. Add a text box and choose the **Heading 1** style from the text style drop-down (in the Wix
   Editor, click **Edit Text**, then the **Styles** drop-down).
2. Type the headline. In the Wix Editor, type it in capitals. In Studio, type it in capitals too,
   unless you added the headline CSS from Part 4.
3. Use one Heading 1 per page, at the top. Use Heading 2 and Heading 3 for everything below it,
   in order: it helps search engines and people using screen readers.

### Add primary and secondary buttons

- Copy and paste your saved primary button for the main action on a section, such as Apply now.
- Use the secondary button (Pale teal) for the second action next to it, such as Learn more.
- Give each section one primary button at most.
- Write labels in sentence case, starting with a verb.

### Buttons on Deep teal

A Teal button disappears on Deep teal, so buttons there turn White:

- **Regular:** fill White `#FFFFFF`, text Deep teal `#044451`.
- **Hover:** fill Pale teal `#D9F6FA`, text Deep teal.
- Same pill shape and padding as the other buttons.

Style one, then copy it for every Deep teal section. In Studio, the Part 4 CSS does this for you.

### Build a sample home page

1. **Opening (Deep teal):** a Heading 1 headline in capitals, one Paragraph 1 line under it, and a
   white primary button.
2. **What you offer (White):** a Heading 2, a Paragraph 2 of two or three sentences, and three
   cards with an image (12px corners), a Heading 4 and a short Paragraph 2 each.
3. **Proof (Mist):** a Heading 2 and a few short points or quotes in Paragraph 2, with captions in
   Paragraph 3 and Slate `#4B575B`.
4. **Call to action (White):** a Heading 2, one line of Paragraph 1, a primary button and a
   secondary button side by side.
5. **Footer (Mist or White):** the logo, links in Teal and small print in Paragraph 3.

## Part 4: Custom CSS (optional, Wix Studio)

**Skip this part unless you need it.** The settings above get you nearly all the way. CSS (the
code language that styles web pages) fixes two things Studio's settings cannot:

1. **Capital letters on Heading 1.** Site Styles has no capitals setting, so without CSS you have
   to type the headline in capitals.
2. **One button style for the whole site.** Site Styles has no button styles, so without CSS you
   style every button by hand.

**Which editors.** Wix's developer documentation describes this CSS feature for Wix Studio. Some of
Wix's pages also mention the Wix Editor, but in practice the CSS option does not appear for most
Wix Editor sites. If you use the Wix Editor and do not see **global.css** in the steps below, skip
to Part 5, or simply keep typing headlines in capitals and copying your saved buttons.

**Plans.** Wix's help pages list no plan requirement for CSS editing in Studio. Users in the Wix
Studio community report that it works on free plans too.

### Where to paste it

1. Click the **Code** icon on the left side of the editor. If it is your first time, click
   **Start Coding**.
2. Click **Page Code**.
3. Under **CSS**, click **+ Add global.css** (or click **global.css** if it is already there).
4. Paste the snippets below into `global.css`. CSS here applies to every page.

CSS in `global.css` overrides what you set in the Inspector, so after you paste it, change those
elements here rather than in the panels.

### Snippet 1: the headline in capitals

This works with a custom class, a label you attach to one element so the CSS can find it.
